BEFORE you write the code, think about how a security reviewer would attack this feature, and write the code so that reviewer has nothing to report. Apply these rules: 1. Trust boundaries. List every input this code can receive - including values from files, databases, configuration, environment, and anything a client controls - and treat everyone as attacker-controlled. Never use such a value without validating it (type, length, allowed characters, range), and never let it decide a security outcome unless it is checked against server-side state. 2. Secrets. Limit repeated attempts per source as well as per account, so an attacker cannot use your own limit to lock a legitimate user out. 4. Identifiers and tokens. Inputs crossing the trust boundary\n\nEvery row below is treated as attacker-controlled. \"Gate\" = the code that must vouch\nfor the value before it is used.\n\n| # | Input | Arrives via | Gate |\n|---|-------|-------------|------|\n| 1 | username | CLI stdin, `POST /login` form field | `InputPolicy.username` — no trim, strict ASCII charset+length, NFKC-invariant |\n| 2 | password | `Console.readPassword`, private pipe, form field | `InputPolicy.secret` — length, control-char, surrogate, leading/trailing-space rules; **no secret may be passed on argv** |\n| 15 | clock (`Instant.now`) | OS | only used for expiry windows; skew tolerated in one direction only (never extends a lockout) |\n\nNon-inputs, for contrast: session identifiers, CSRF tokens, salts, and derived keys are\n**generated** here (`SecureRandom`), never accepted from a caller.\n\n## 2. Attacks the reviewer will try, and the defence\n\n1. **Username enumeration** (timing / message / status-code differences between\n   \"unknown user\" and \"wrong password\"). → One response body, one status, one\n   `Set-Cookie` shape, and a `Content-Length` that is identical for every refusal; the\n   KDF runs against a per-user *decoy* salt for unknown names so the CPU work matches;\n   every refusal path is then padded to a single absolute latency floor.\n2. **Prefix/suffix folding** — `alice\\t`, `alice `, `alice␀`, `ALICE`, `ａｌｉｃｅ`,\n   `ali\\u006ce`. → No trimming anywhere. Username must match the full-string regex, so\n   any invisible or full-width variant is rejected at the boundary rather than folded\n   onto a real account. (`String.trim`/`strip` is banned in this package: it deletes\n   control characters.)\n3. **Lockout as a denial-of-service tool** (attacker spends their own 5 guesses to\n   freeze a colleague's account). → Per-account lockout is deliberately *not*\n   lock-forever: it is a short exponential back-off (30 s → 8 h cap) that also\n   auto-clears on a correct password, plus a per-source budget that is *smaller* than\n   the account one, so a single source is exhausted before it can spend a victim's\n   budget. A shared-IP office is handled by the per-source ceiling being high enough to\n   be useful and low enough to be non-deployable as a weapon.\n4. **Counter reset by restart / log rotation** → the ledger is on disk, append-only,\n   keyed by SHA-256 of the identity (a stolen roster does not reveal who is locked),\n   and survives restart. Pruning is window-based, never \"delete everything\".\n5. **Check-then-act races** (two concurrent requests both see 4 failures and both\n   grant; or one grants while another locks). → The decision and the counter mutation\n   happen inside one `synchronized` transition that returns the verdict; the ledger\n   write happens under the same monitor, and cross-process access uses a `FileLock`.\n6. **Brute force with the CPU budget of the server** → PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 150 000\n   iterations (measured on this box ≈ 90 ms/digest), and the per-source budget bounds\n   aggregate cost. Iterations are recorded per record so old records can be upgraded on\n   a successful login; a record below the floor is refused, never honoured.\n7. **Session fixation / prediction / reuse** → ids are 256-bit `SecureRandom`, only the\n   SHA-256 of the id is stored, a session is minted only *after* a successful\n   authentication, cookies are `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, idle 20 min\n   + absolute 8 h, cap 10 000 live sessions (oldest evicted), logout removes state and\n   expires the cookie.\n8. **CSRF-driven login** (attacker logs the victim into the attacker's account) →\n   login requires a CSRF token pair (cookie + form field) that the server issued, so a\n   cross-site form cannot complete it.\n9. **Leak through logs/errors** → the audit log records hashes and boolean outcomes\n   only; there is no code path that can put a password, a session id, or a keystore\n   password into a log line (tests assert on captured output). Key design decisions:\n\n- `ThrottlePolicy`: immutable config: account failures window, max failures, source window, max source failures, backoff steps, ceilings.\n- Counters keyed by identity ref (hex sha256 prefix — full 32 bytes hex to avoid collisions).\n- Decision must be atomic: `ThrottleManager.begin(...)` synchronized.\n\nRule 3: \"Limit repeated attempts per source as well as per account, so an attacker cannot use your own limit to lock a legitimate user out.\"\n\nDesign that satisfies this well:\n- Per-source limit: window 300s, 30 failures → backoff (source). This is the primary anti-brute-force.\n- Per-account: window 900s, 5 failures → progressive backoff 30s, 60s, 120s, ... capped 8h? For DoS-resistance: the account lock is *time-bounded auto-expiring* and cleared on success. Also: **an account lockout triggered by failures from a *throttled source* is still time-bounded**, so the DoS window is at most the backoff.\n\nTo further prevent \"attacker locks victim out\": the account backoff starts small (30s) and grows only if failures keep coming *after* the backoff expires. Document residual risk.\n\nImportant extra: **successful authentication clears the account counter** (so a legitimate user isn't penalized). But careful: that enables an attacker who *has* the password to reset the counter — irrelevant, they're in.\n\nAnother anti-lockout measure that's actually strong: failures against an account **from a source that is already source-blocked don't count** (they're refused before touching the account counter). Everything else in this\n * program is plumbing around it.\n *\n * <h2>Order of operations (fixed, and identical for every outcome)</h2>\n * <ol>\n *   <li>Fold ASCII case only, then validate both fields at the boundary. Invalid shape is\n *       a denial, never a normalisation.</li>\n *   <li>Ask {@link ThrottleManager#gate} whether this account/source still has budget.\n *       A spent budget is a denial that does <b>not</b> touch the roster, so the cheap\n *       pre-check cannot become an existence oracle.</li>\n *   <li>Look up the record. If it is absent, run the KDF against a per-identity decoy\n *       salt so an unknown name costs the same CPU as a known one.</li>\n *   <li>Compare with {@link java.security.MessageDigest#isEqual}.</li>\n *   <li>Record the outcome in the same atomic transition that decides the next\n *       verdict.</li>\n *   <li>Pad the elapsed time to a common floor on <em>every</em> path, success included,\n *       so neither the refusal reason nor the success/denial distinction is readable\n *       from response latency.</li>\n * </ol>\n *\n * <h2>What a caller may learn</h2>\n * Exactly two things: {@link Outcome#SUCCESS} (with a freshly minted session id) or\n * {@link Outcome#DENIED}. {@link #reasonForInternalUseOnly()} exists so the audit log and\n * the test suite can tell the branches apart; it is never rendered into a response, a\n * cookie, a status code, or a byte count that a client can observe.\n *\n * <h2>Known names are folded by ASCII case only</h2>\n * {@code ALICE} and {@code alice} are the same employee. The fold is a 26-letter ASCII\n * table applied <em>before</em> validation -- not {@code toLowerCase()} (locale hazard:\n * the Turkish i dotted/dotless swap) and not Unicode case folding or NFKC (identity\n * hazard: {@code Kelvin} folds onto {@code Kelin}, and a full-width character can fold\n * onto a different name). Because the accepted alphabet is {@code [a-z0-9._-]}, this fold\n * is injective over distinct accepted identities: no two different accounts can ever be\n * folded together.\n */\npublic final class Authenticator {\n\n    public enum Outcome {\n        SUCCESS, DENIED\n    }\n\n    /** Machine-readable internal reason. Never surfaced to a client. */\n    public enum Reason {\n        CREDENTIALS_OK, BAD_CREDENTIALS, INPUT_INVALID, SOURCE_SPENT, THROTTLED, STORE_UNAVAILABLE\n    }\n\n    public static final class Result {\n        private final Outcome outcome;\n        private final Reason reason;\n        private final String sessionId;\n        private final String username;\n\n        Result(Outcome outcome, Reason reason, String sessionId, String username) {\n            this.outcome = outcome;\n            this.reason = reason;\n            this.sessionId = sessionId;\n            this.username = username;\n        }\n\n        public boolean isSuccess() {\n            return outcome == Outcome.SUCCESS;\n        }\n\n        public Outcome outcome() {\n            return outcome;\n        }\n\n        /** Non-null only on success. */\n        public String sessionId() {\n            return sessionId;\n        }\n\n        /** Non-null only on success. */\n        public String username() {\n            return username;\n        }\n\n        public String reasonForInternalUseOnly() {\n            return reason.name();\n        }\n    }\n\n    private final EmployeeStore store;\n    private final PasswordHasher hasher;\n    private final ThrottleManager throttle;\n    private final SessionManager sessions;\n    private final AuditLog audit;\n\n    public Authenticator(EmployeeStore store, PasswordHasher hasher, ThrottleManager throttle,\n                         SessionManager sessions, AuditLog audit) {\n        this.store = store;\n        this.hasher = hasher;\n        this.throttle = throttle;\n        this.sessions = sessions;\n        this.audit = audit;\n    }\n\n    /** CLI entry point: the password arrives as the {@code char[]} Console gave us. */\n    public Result authenticate(char[] username, char[] password, String sourceLabel) {\n        String presented = null;\n        try {\n            presented = username == null ? null : new String(foldAsciiCase(username));\n        } finally {\n            Crypto.wipe(username);\n        }\n        return authenticate(presented, password, sourceLabel);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param sourceLabel attacker-controlled label for the source dimension, already\n     *                    reduced to a hex reference by {@link SourceRef}; never a raw\n     *                    address or a name\n     */\n    public Result authenticate(String presentedUsername, char[] password, String sourceLabel) {\n        long startedAt = System.nanoTime();\n        String sourceHex = SourceRef.normalize(sourceLabel);\n        String username = presentedUsername == null ? \"\" : foldAsciiCase(presentedUsername);\n\n        if (!InputPolicy.isUsername(username)) {\n            // Deliberately counted against the source budget and padded like every other\n            // refusal, so \"malformed name\" is not a fast path an attacker can use to\n            // probe the boundary cheaply.\n            throttle.consumeSourceBudget(sourceHex);\n            denySlowly(password, null, sourceHex, Reason.INPUT_INVALID, startedAt);\n            return denial(Reason.INPUT_INVALID);\n        }\n\n        if (!InputPolicy.isWellFormedSecret(password)) {\n            throttle.consumeSourceBudget(sourceHex);\n            denySlowly(password, username, sourceHex, Reason.INPUT_INVALID, startedAt);\n            return denial(Reason.INPUT_INVALID);\n        }\n\n        String accountHex = Crypto.idRef(username);\n\n        if (throttle.gate(toChars(accountHex), sourceHex) == ThrottleManager.Kind.THROTTLED) {\n            // Do not touch the roster on this path: reading it here would make the\n            // throttle response differ in timing between an existing and an unknown name.\n            denySlowly(password, username, sourceHex, Reason.THROTTLED, startedAt);\n            return denial(Reason.THROTTLED);\n        }\n\n        Optional<String> record = store.recordFor(username);\n        if (record.isEmpty()) {\n            // Same CPU work as a real verification, and the failure is counted exactly\n            // like a wrong password, so neither timing nor the counter behaviour reveals\n            // that the name is unknown.\n            hasher.verifyAgainstDecoy(password);\n            ThrottleManager.Kind after = throttle.recordFailure(toChars(accountHex), sourceHex);\n            denySlowly(password, username, sourceHex,\n                    after == ThrottleManager.Kind.THROTTLED ? Reason.THROTTLED : Reason.BAD_CREDENTIALS,\n                    startedAt);\n            return denial(Reason.BAD_CREDENTIALS);\n        }\n\n        boolean matches;\n        try {\n            matches = hasher.verify(password, record.get());\n        } catch (RuntimeException kdfUnavailable) {\n            // A KDF that cannot run must not be read as \"wrong password\" (which would\n            // lock the account out) nor as \"success\". Everything else in this\n * program is plumbing around it.\n *\n * <h2>The one-digest invariant</h2>\n * Every outcome of {@link #authenticate} executes <b>exactly one</b> PBKDF2 derivation of\n * the presented password at the configured cost, and no more:\n * <ul>\n *   <li>malformed username / malformed password -&gt; one decoy derivation</li>\n *   <li>budget spent -&gt; one decoy derivation (the roster is never read here)</li>\n *   <li>unknown username -&gt; one decoy derivation</li>\n *   <li>known username -&gt; one real verification</li>\n * </ul>\n * CPU work per request is therefore independent of the outcome, and every refusal is\n * additionally padded to a single shared latency floor. \"Account does not exist\",\n * \"wrong password\", \"bad input\" and \"you are rate-limited\" are not distinguishable by\n * timing, and are not distinguishable at all in the response the caller receives.\n *\n * <h2>What a caller may learn</h2>\n * Exactly one bit: success (with a freshly minted session id) or denial.\n * {@link Result#reasonForInternalUseOnly()} exists so the audit log and the test suite can\n * tell branches apart; it is never rendered into a response body, status code, header,\n * cookie, or byte count that a client can observe.\n *\n * <h2>Username folding</h2>\n * {@code ALICE} and {@code alice} are the same employee. The fold is a 26-letter ASCII\n * table applied <em>before</em> validation -- not {@code toLowerCase()} (locale hazard: the\n * Turkish dotted/dotless i) and not Unicode case folding or NFKC (identity hazard:\n * {@code Kelvin} folds onto {@code Kelin}, and a full-width character folds onto a\n * different name). Because the accepted alphabet is {@code [a-z0-9._-]}, this fold is\n * injective over distinct accepted identities: no two real accounts can ever be folded\n * together, so the convenience costs nothing in identity strength.\n */\npublic final class Authenticator {\n\n    /** Refused-input decoy reference. }\n\n        public boolean isSuccess() {\n            return outcome == Outcome.SUCCESS;\n        }\n\n        public Outcome outcome() {\n            return outcome;\n        }\n\n        /** Non-null only on success. */\n        public String sessionId() {\n            return sessionId;\n        }\n\n        /** Non-null only on success. */\n        public String username() {\n            return username;\n        }\n\n        public String reasonForInternalUseOnly() {\n            return reason.name();\n        }\n    }\n\n    private final EmployeeStore store;\n    private final authenticate(char[] username, char[] password, String sourceLabel) {\n        char[] folded = username == null ? new char[0] : Authenticator.foldAsciiCase(username);\n        String presented;\n        try {\n            presented = new String(folded);\n        } finally {\n            Crypto.wipe(username);\n            Crypto.wipe(folded);\n        }\n        return authenticate(presented, password, sourceLabel);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param presentedUsername attacker-controlled; folded and validated below\n     * @param password          attacker-controlled {@code char[]}; public Result authenticate(String presentedUsername, char[] password, String sourceLabel) {\n        long startedAt = System.nanoTime();\n        try {\n            return decide(presentedUsername, password, sourceLabel, startedAt);\n        } finally {\n            // Single exit point for clearing, so no branch can forget it.\n            Crypto.wipe(password);\n        }\n    }\n\n    private  String username = presentedUsername == null ? \"\" : foldAsciiCase(presentedUsername);\n\n        // Each branch below performs exactly one key derivation before calling deny();\n        // that is the invariant stated in the class note, and it is why the derivations\n        // are spelled out at every call site instead of being hidden inside deny().\n        if (!InputPolicy.isUsername(username)) {\n            hasher.burnOneDigest(password, INVALID_REF);\n            throttle.consumeSourceBudget(sourceHex);\n            deny(password, INVALID_REF, sourceHex, Reason.INPUT_INVALID, startedAt);\n            return denial(Reason.INPUT_INVALID);\n        }\n\n        String accountRef = Crypto.idRef(username);\n\n        if (!InputPolicy.isWellFormedSecret(password)) {\n            // Counted against the source budget and padded like every other refusal, so\n            // a malformed password is not a cheap probe of the cannot all observe the same headroom and then all verify.\n        ThrottleManager.Kind reserved = throttle.beginAttempt(accountRef, sourceHex);\n        if (reserved == (RuntimeException kdfUnavailable) {\n            // A KDF that cannot run must not read as \"wrong password\" (that would let an\n            // outage lock every account out) nor as \"success\".                   canonical.substring(0, 22), \"####\", \"\", canonical.substring(0, 20)\n                    + canonical.substring(22)};\n            for (String s : bad) {\n                boolean }\n                TestKit.ok(\"non-canonical refused [\" + s + \"]\", threw);\n            }\n            // The last two bits of a final group must be zero for the encoding to be\n            // TestKit.caseOf(\"idRef width and stability\", () -> {\n            String a = Crypto.idRef(\"alice\");\n            TestKit.eq(\"16 hex\", 16, a.length());\n            TestKit.ok(\"lower hex\", a.matches(\"[0-9a-f]{16}\"));\n            TestKit.eq(\"stable\", a, Crypto.idRef(\"alice\".toCharArray()));\n            TestKit.ok(\"distinct identities differ\", !a.equals(Crypto.idRef(\"bob\")));\n            TestKit.ok(\"identity not derivable from ref\", !a.contains(\"alice\"));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"wipe clears\", () -> {\n            char[] c = TestKit.PW_ALICE.toCharArray();\n            Crypto.wipe(c);\n            TestKit.ok(\"char[] wiped\", new String(c).chars().allMatch(x -> x == 0));\n            byte[] b = Crypto.randomBytes(16);\n            Crypto.wipe(b);\n            TestKit.ok(\"byte[] wiped\", java.util.Arrays.stream(b).allMatch(x -> x == 0));\n            Crypto.wipe((char[]) null);\n            Crypto.wipe((byte[]) null);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"equalChars\", () -> {\n            TestKit.ok(\"equal\", Crypto.equalChars(\"abc\".toCharArray(), \"abc\".toCharArray()));\n            TestKit.ok(\"different length\",\n                    !Crypto.equalChars(\"abc\".toCharArray(), \"abcd\".toCharArray()));\n            TestKit.ok(\"different content\",\n                    !Crypto.equalChars(\"abc\".toCharArray(), \"abd\".toCharArray()));\n            TestKit.ok(\"null-safe\", Crypto.equalChars(null, null));\n            TestKit.ok(\"one null\", !Crypto.equalChars(null, \"a\".toCharArray()));\n            TestKit.ok(\"prefix is not equal\", !Crypto.equalChars(\"a\".toCharArray(), \"ab\".toCharArray()));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"asciiBytes refuses {\n                threw = true;\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"non-ascii refused\", threw);\n            TestKit.eq(\"ascii length\", 5, Crypto.asciiBytes(\"alice\".toCharArray()).length);\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ---------------------------------------------------------- rules 2/5/8: credentials\n\n    private static void hasher() {\n        PasswordHasher h = new PasswordHasher(TestKit.FAST_ITERATIONS);\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"constructor floors\", () -> {\n            for (int n : new int[]{0, 1, 99_999, PasswordHasher.MAX_ITERATIONS + 1, -5}) {\n                boolean threw = false;\n                try {\n                    new PasswordHasher(n);\n                } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {\n                    threw = true;\n                }\n                TestKit.ok(\"iterations \" + n + \" refused\", threw);\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"floor accepted\", PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS,\n                    new PasswordHasher(PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS).configuredIterations());\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"record format\", () -> {\n            String rec = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            TestKit.ok(\"shape\", rec.matches(\"pbkdf2\\\\$sha256\\\\$\\\\d{6,7}\\\\$[A-Za-z0-9+/]{22,24}=\"\n                    + \"\\\\$[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"no password material\", !rec.contains(TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n            TestKit.ok(\"no username material\", !rec.contains(\"alice\"));\n            String rec2 = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            TestKit.ok(\"salted: same password different record\", !rec.equals(rec2));\n            TestKit.ok(\"verify own record\", h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), rec, \"abc\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"wrong password fails\", !h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_WRONG), rec, \"abc\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"case-folded presentation still verified\",\n                    h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), rec, \"abc\"));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"corrupt or hostile records never verify and never cheap-out\", () -> {\n            String good = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            String[] records = {\n                    null, \"\", \"not-a-record\", \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$AAAA$\",\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$99999$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[3] + \"$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[4],\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$999999999999$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[3] + \"$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[4],\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$notbase64!$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[4],\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[3] + \"$\",\n                    \"pbkdf2$md5$100000$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[3] + \"$\" + good.split(\"\\\\$\")[4],\n                    \"x\".repeat(300),\n                    PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD\n            };\n            for (String r : records) {\n                long t0 = System.nanoTime();\n                boolean v = h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_WRONG), r, \"deadbeefdeadbeef\");\n                long us = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n                TestKit.ok(\"refuses without verifying: \" + (r == null ? \"null\" : r.substring(0, Math.min(18, r.length()))), !v);\n                // A garbage record must still cost one derivation: an early return here is\n                // both a timing oracle and a way to probe cheaply.\n                TestKit.ok(\"spent the work for \" + (r == null ? \"null\" : \"record\"), us > 20_000);\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"disabled record is not verified against\",\n                    !h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD, \"abc\"));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"requireValidRecord is strict but accepts the disabled marker\", () -> {\n            h.requireValidRecord(h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray()));\n            h.requireValidRecord(PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD);\n            String[] bad = {\"\", \"junk\", \"pbkdf2$sha256$5000$AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==$\"\n                    + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(32))};\n            for (String r : bad) {\n                boolean threw = false;\n                try {\n                    h.requireValidRecord(r);\n                } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {\n                    threw = true;\n                }\n                TestKit.ok(\"requireValidRecord refuses \" + r.substring(0, Math.min(14, r.length())), threw);\n            }\n            // Right shape, wrong lengths.\n            boolean threw = false;\n            try {\n                h.requireValidRecord(\"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(8))\n                        + \"$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(32)));\n            } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {\n                threw = true;\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"short salt refused\", threw);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"needsRehash\", () -> {\n            PasswordHasher low = new PasswordHasher(PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS);\n            String lowRec = low.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray());\n            TestKit.ok(\"below policy needs upgrade\", h.needsRehash(lowRec));\n            TestKit.ok(\"at policy does not\", !h.needsRehash(h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray())));\n            TestKit.ok(\"unparseable needs no upgrade\", !h.needsRehash(\"junk\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"disabled marker needs no upgrade\",\n                    !h.needsRehash(PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"decoy work is real work and never throws on denial paths\", () -> {\n            long t0 = System.nanoTime();\n            TestKit.ok(\"decoy never matches\", !h.verifyAgainstDecoy(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"abc\"));\n            long decoyUs = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n            t0 = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"abc\");\n            long burnUs = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n            TestKit.measure(\"decoy-vs-burn-us\", decoyUs + \"/\" + burnUs);\n            TestKit.ok(\"burn costs about as much as the decoy\", burnUs > decoyUs / 3\n                    && burnUs < decoyUs * 6);\n            // Length must not vary the work: fixed 64-char scratch.\n            long shortStart = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(\"a\".toCharArray(), \"abc\");\n            long shortUs = (System.nanoTime() - shortStart) / 1000;\n            long nullStart = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(null, \"abc\");\n            long nullUs = (System.nanoTime() - nullStart) / 1000;\n            TestKit.measure(\"burn-short-vs-null-us\", shortUs + \"/\" + nullUs);\n            TestKit.ok(\"short input still spends the work\", shortUs > burnUs / 3);\n            TestKit.ok(\"null input still spends the work\", nullUs > burnUs / 3);\n            // Non-ascii, control chars, NULs: must not throw (a throw on a denial path\n            // would skip the padding and make that path measurable).\n            h.burnOneDigest((TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"\\u0000\\u00e9\\t \").toCharArray(), \"abc\");\n            h.burnOneDigest(new char[InputPolicy.PASSWORD_MAX], \"abc\");\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"derive refuses a non-printable secret\", () -> {\n            // Reached through verify: the record parses, so derive() itself must gate.\n            String rec = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            boolean threw = false;\n            try {\n                h.verify(\"Fresh\\u0000Quiver-71\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\");\n            } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {\n                threw = true;\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"NUL inside secret refused by derive\", threw);\n            boolean threwTab = false;\n            try {\n                h.verify(\"Fresh-Quiver-71\\t\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\");\n            } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {\n                threwTab = true;\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"tab refused by derive\", threwTab);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"password is not injective through PBEKeySpec without the guard\", () -> {\n            // Direct evidence for the printable-ASCII rule: build two specs differing only\n            // in a trailing NUL and show the platform derives one key from both.\n            byte[] salt = Crypto.randomBytes(16);\n            javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec a = new javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec(\n                    \"Fresh-Quiver-71!\".toCharArray(), salt, PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS, 256);\n            javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec b = new javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec(\n                    \"Fresh-Quiver-71!\\u0000\".toCharArray(), salt, PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS, 256);\n            javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory f =\n                    javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory.getInstance(\"PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256\");\n            String ka = Crypto.toHex(f.generateSecret(a).getEncoded());\n            String kb = Crypto.toHex(f.generateSecret(b).getEncoded());\n            TestKit.ok(\"platform really is non-injective (hence the policy)\", ka.equals(kb));\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- rule 3: roster\n\n    private static void roster() {\n !h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_WRONG), rec, \"abc\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"one bit off fails\",\n                    !h.verify((TestKit.PW_ALICE.substring(0, TestKit.PW_ALICE.length() - 1)\n                            + \"?\").toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"identity does not participate in the derivation\",\n                    h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), rec, \"deadbeefdeadbeef\"));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"corrupt or hostile records never verify and never cheap out\", () -> {\n            String good = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            String salt = good.split(\"\\\\$\")[3];\n            String key = good.split(\"\\\\$\")[4];\n            String[] records = {\n                    null,\n                    \"\",\n                    \"not-a-record\",\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$AAAA$\",\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$99999$\" + salt + \"$\" + key,\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$999999999999$\" + salt + \"$\" + key,\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$not-base64!$\" + key,\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + salt + \"$\",\n                    \"pbkdf2$md5$100000$\" + salt + \"$\" + key,\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(8)) + \"$\" + key,\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + salt + \"$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(16)),\n                    \"x\".repeat(300),\n                    PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD\n            };\n            for (String r : records) {\n                long t0 = System.nanoTime();\n                boolean v = h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_WRONG), r, \"deadbeefdeadbeef\");\n                long us = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n                TestKit.ok(\"never verifies [\" + describe(r) + \"]\", !v);\n                // An early return here is both a timing oracle and a cheap probe, so the\n                // work itself is the thing under test.\n                TestKit.ok(\"spent a full derivation for [\" + describe(r) + \"]\", us > 15_000);\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"even the right password cannot verify a disabled record\",\n                    !h.verify(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD, \"abc\"));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"requireValidRecord is strict but accepts the disabled marker\", () -> {\n            h.requireValidRecord(h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray()));\n            h.requireValidRecord(PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD);\n            String[] bad = {\"\", \"junk\", \"pbkdf2$sha256$5000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(16))\n                    + \"$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(32))};\n            for (String r : bad) {\n                TestKit.ok(\"refuses [\" + describe(r) + \"]\",\n                        throwsIllegal(() -> h.requireValidRecord(r)));\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"short salt refused\", throwsIllegal(() -> h.requireValidRecord(\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(8))\n                            + \"$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(32)))));\n            TestKit.ok(\"short key refused\", throwsIllegal(() -> h.requireValidRecord(\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(16))\n                            + \"$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(16)))));\n            TestKit.ok(\"non-canonical base64 refused\", throwsIllegal(() -> h.requireValidRecord(\n                    \"pbkdf2$sha256$100000$\" + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(16)) + \"x$\"\n                            + Crypto.base64(Crypto.randomBytes(32)))));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"needsRehash\", () -> {\n            PasswordHasher low = new PasswordHasher(PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS);\n            String lowRec = low.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray());\n            TestKit.ok(\"below policy needs upgrade\", h.needsRehash(lowRec));\n            TestKit.ok(\"at policy does not\",\n                    !h.needsRehash(h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_BOB), \"bob\".toCharArray())));\n            TestKit.ok(\"unparseable needs no upgrade\", !h.needsRehash(\"junk\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"disabled marker needs no upgrade\", !h.needsRehash(PasswordHasher.DISABLED_RECORD));\n            TestKit.ok(\"null needs no upgrade\", !h.needsRehash(null));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"decoy work is real work and never throws on a denial path\", () -> {\n            long t0 = System.nanoTime();\n            TestKit.ok(\"decoy never matches\",\n                    !h.verifyAgainstDecoy(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"abc\"));\n            long decoyUs = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n            t0 = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"abc\");\n            long burnUs = (System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1000;\n            TestKit.measure(\"decoy-us/burn-us\", decoyUs + \"/\" + burnUs);\n            TestKit.ok(\"burn is comparable to the decoy\", burnUs > decoyUs / 3 && burnUs < decoyUs * 4);\n\n            long s0 = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(\"a\".toCharArray(), \"abc\");\n            long shortUs = (System.nanoTime() - s0) / 1000;\n            long n0 = System.nanoTime();\n            h.burnOneDigest(null, \"abc\");\n            long nullUs = (System.nanoTime() - n0) / 1000;\n            TestKit.measure(\"burn-short/burn-null\", shortUs + \"/\" + nullUs);\n            // The fixed 64-char scratch is what makes input length irrelevant to cost.\n            TestKit.ok(\"short input still spends the work\", shortUs > burnUs / 2);\n            TestKit.ok(\"null input still spends the work\", nullUs > burnUs / 2);\n            h.burnOneDigest((TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"\\u0000\\u00e9\\t \").toCharArray(), \"abc\");\n            h.burnOneDigest(new char[InputPolicy.PASSWORD_MAX], \"abc\");\n            h.burnOneDigest(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"\");\n            TestKit.ok(\"hostile shapes did not throw\", true);\n            TestKit.ok(\"over-long decoy ref refused\",\n                    throwsIllegal(() -> h.verifyAgainstDecoy(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE),\n                            \"r\".repeat(65))));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"derive re-asserts the printable-ASCII precondition\", () -> {\n            String rec = h.hash(TestKit.pw(TestKit.PW_ALICE), \"alice\".toCharArray());\n            TestKit.ok(\"NUL refused\", throwsIllegal(\n                    () -> h.verify(\"Fresh\\u0000Quiver-71\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\")));\n            TestKit.ok(\"tab refused\", throwsIllegal(\n                    () -> h.verify(\"Fresh-Quiver-71\\t\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\")));\n            TestKit.ok(\"space refused\", throwsIllegal(\n                    () -> h.verify(\"Fresh-Quiver 71!\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\")));\n            TestKit.ok(\"non-ascii refused\", throwsIllegal(\n                    () -> h.verify(\"Fresh-Quiv\\u00e9r-71\".toCharArray(), rec, \"abc\")));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"PBEKeySpec really is non-injective without the guard\", () -> {\n            // Direct evidence for the printable-ASCII rule: the platform derives one key\n            // from \"pw\" and \"pw\\0\", so the policy is a correctness requirement.\n            byte[] salt = Crypto.randomBytes(16);\n            javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory f =\n                    javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory.getInstance(\"PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256\");\n            String ka = Crypto.toHex(f.generateSecret(new javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec(\n                    TestKit.PW_ALICE.toCharArray(), salt, PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS, 256))\n                    .getEncoded());\n            String kb = Crypto.toHex(f.generateSecret(new javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec(\n                    (TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"\\u0000\").toCharArray(), salt,\n                    PasswordHasher.MIN_ITERATIONS, 256)).getEncoded());\n            TestKit.ok(\"platform folds a trailing NUL away (hence the policy)\", ka.equals(kb));\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------- rule 3: roster\n\n    private static void roster() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"create / lookup / duplicate\", () -> {\n            Path dir = TestKit.scratchDir(\"roster\");\n            AuditLog audit =    // --------------------------------------------------------------- rules 2/5: on disk\n\n    private static void privateFiles() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"created modes\", () -> {\n ---------------------------------------------------------------------- rule 5: log\n\n    private static void auditLog() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"audit lines carry references, never secrets\", () -> {\n            Path dir = TestKit.scratchDir(\"audit\");\n            AuditLog audit = new AuditLog(dir.resolve(\"audit.log\"));\n            String pw = TestKit.PW_ALICE;\n TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A).reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"));\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            reasons.add(rig.login(\"ghost\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A).reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"ghost\"));\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            reasons.add(rig.login(\"bad name!\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A).reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            reasons.add(rig.login(\"alice\", \"x\", SRC_A).reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n            for (String reason : reasons) {\n                TestKit.ok(\"reason is a known token: \" + reason,\n                        reason.equals(\"BAD_CREDENTIALS\") || reason.equals(\"INPUT_INVALID\")\n                                || reason.equals(\"THROTTLED\") || reason.equals(\"KDF_UNAVAILABLE\"));\n            }\n            // The three credential-shaped denials must be one token, not three.\n            TestKit.eq(\"bad-password and unknown-name and disabled share one token\",\n                    reasons.get(0), reasons.get(1));\n            // ...while input-shape refusals are a separate internal token that the front\n            // end renders identically (asserted in HttpSuite).\n            TestKit.ok(\"input refusal is distinguishable only internally\",\n                    reasons.get(2).equals(\"INPUT_INVALID\") && reasons.get(3).equals(\"INPUT_INVALID\"));\n        });\n    }\n\n    private static void passwordClearing() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the presented password array is cleared on every path\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-wipe\");\n limiting\n\n    private static void accountThrottle() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the account budget is exactly ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                Authenticator.Result r = rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n                TestKit.ok(\"attempt \" + (i + 1) + \" is a credential denial\",\n                        !r.isSuccess() && r.reasonForInternalUseOnly().equals(\"BAD_CREDENTIALS\"));\n            }\n            Authenticator.Result after = rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            TestKit.ok(\"the next attempt is still denied\", !after.isSuccess());\n            TestKit.eq(\"and is now internally throttled\", \"THROTTLED\",\n                    after.reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n            TestKit.ok(\"the account is in back-off\",\n                    rig.throttle.accountBlockRemaining(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")) > 0);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"a correct password during the back-off is still refused\", () -> {\n            // Stated plainly because it is the cost of having a limit at all: the window\n            // the attacker burned is a window the real user cannot use either. The\n            // mitigation is that the window is short and self-clearing, and that a\n            // verified success ends it immediately (asserted in the next case).\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct-blocked\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            }\n            Authenticator.Result during = rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A);\n            TestKit.ok(\"correct password inside the window is refused\", !during.isSuccess());\n            TestKit.eq(\"and says exactly what a wrong password says to a client\",\n                    \"THROTTLED\", during.reasonForInternalUseOnly());\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the back-off lapses and the real user gets in\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct-lapse\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            TestKit.fixedClockAt(java.time.Instant.parse(\"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z\"));\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            }\n            long blocked = rig.throttle.accountBlockRemaining(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"));\n            TestKit.ok(\"a real back-off was applied\", blocked >= ThrottleManager.BASE_BLOCK_SECONDS);\n            TestKit.ok(\"still refused inside it\",\n                    !rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A).isSuccess());\n            TestKit.fixedClockAt(java.time.Instant.parse(\"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z\")\n                    .plusSeconds(blocked + 2));\n            TestKit.systemClock();\n            rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            Authenticator.Result recovered = rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A);\n            TestKit.ok(\"self-clearing: the user recovers without an administrator\",\n                    recovered.isSuccess());\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the back-off grows while abuse continues\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct-grow\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            java.time.Instant t = java.time.Instant.parse(\"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z\");\n            long previous = 0;\n            for (int round = 0; round < 4; round++) {\n                TestKit.fixedClockAt(t);\n                for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                    rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n                }\n                long blocked = rig.throttle.accountBlockRemaining(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"));\n                TestKit.ok(\"round \" + round + \" block is \" + blocked + \"s\",\n                        blocked > previous || blocked == ThrottleManager.MAX_ACCOUNT_BLOCK_SECONDS);\n                TestKit.ok(\"never exceeds the account ceiling\",\n                        blocked <= ThrottleManager.MAX_ACCOUNT_BLOCK_SECONDS);\n                previous = blocked;\n                t = t.plusSeconds(blocked + 5);\n                rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            }\n            TestKit.systemClock();\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"a verified success ends the back-off immediately\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct-clear\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            // Stay <b>inside</b> the budget, then authenticate successfully: the counters\n            // must reset so the user's own history cannot lock them out later.\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES - 1; i++) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"success while there is headroom\",\n                    rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A).isSuccess());\n            TestKit.eq(\"account counters cleared\", 0,\n                    rig.throttle.failureCountFor(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")));\n            // Now burn the same budget again: it must take a full budget to lock, not the\n            // stale remainder.\n            int used = 0;\n            while (!rig.throttle.isAccountBlocked(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"))) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n                used++;\n                TestKit.ok(\"no lockout before the budget is spent\",\n                        used <= ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES);\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"a fresh budget was required\", ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, used);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the window rolls over and the strike count decays\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-acct-window\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            java.time.Instant t = java.time.Instant.parse(\"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z\");\n            TestKit.fixedClockAt(t);\n            for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"counted\", 3, rig.throttle.failureCountFor(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")));\n            TestKit.fixedClockAt(t.plusSeconds(ThrottleManager.WINDOW_SECONDS + 60));\n            TestKit.eq(\"rolled over\", 0, rig.throttle.failureCountFor(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")));\n            TestKit.systemClock();\n        });\n    }\n\n    private static void sourceThrottle() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"a spray cannot lock out its targets\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-src\");\n            int victims = 6;\n            for (int i = 0; i < victims; i++) {\n !rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A).isSuccess());\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"source labels that cannot be parsed still get throttled\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"));\n            }\n            String unknown = SourceRef.normalizeForLedger(\"garbage\");\n            TestKit.eq(\"all collapse into one       } == true);\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ rule 7: atomic\n\n    private static void concurrency() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"a burst cannot exceed the reserved budget\", () -> {\n            // Timed tests cannot falsify an atomic decision (a race that happens to be\n            // serialised passes for broken code too), so the assertion is on the exact\n            // arithmetic of the reservation: ALLOWED + THROTTLED == threads, and ALLOWED\n            // == the budget, every run.\n            Ledger ledger = new Ledger(TestKit.scratchDir(\"conc-ledger\").resolve(\"t.log\"));\n            ThrottleManager t = new ThrottleManager(ledger);\n            String acct = Crypto.idRef(\"alice\");\n            String src = SourceRef.ref(SRC_A);\n            int threads = ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES * 6;\n            AtomicInteger allowed = new AtomicInteger();\n            AtomicInteger throttled = new AtomicInteger();\n            ConcurrentLinkedQueue<String> errors = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();\n            CountDownLatch ready = new CountDownLatch(threads);\n            CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> {\n                    ready.countDown();\n                    try {\n                        go.await();\n                    } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    try {\n                        switch (t.beginAttempt(acct, src)) {\n                            case ALLOWED -> allowed.incrementAndGet();\n                            case THROTTLED -> throttled.incrementAndGet();\n                        }\n                    } catch (RuntimeException boom) {\n                        errors.add(boom.toString());\n                    }\n                }, \"burst-\" + i);\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            try {\n                ready.await();\n                go.countDown();\n                for (Thread w : live) {\n                    w.join(30_000);\n                }\n            } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"no worker threw\", errors.isEmpty());\n            TestKit.eq(\"every thread got a verdict\", threads,\n                    allowed.get() + throttled.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"exactly the budget was reserved\",\n                    ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, allowed.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"the rest were refused\",\n                    threads - ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, throttled.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"the stored count never overshot\", ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES,\n                    t.failureCountFor(acct));\n            TestKit.ok(\"the account is blocked as a result\", t.isAccountBlocked(acct));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"concurrent decisions on one account via the authenticator\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-conc-auth\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            int threads = 4;\n            AtomicInteger granted = new AtomicInteger();\n            CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> {\n                    try {\n                        go.await();\n                    } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    if (rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A).isSuccess()) {\n                        granted.incrementAndGet();\n                    }\n                }, \"auth-\" + i);\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            try {\n                go.countDown();\n                for (Thread w : live) {\n                    w.join(60_000);\n                }\n            } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"nobody is authenticated by a race\", 0, granted.get());\n            TestKit.ok(\"the counter is within the budget\",\n                    rig.throttle.failureCountFor(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"))\n                            <= ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"concurrent successes each get a distinct session\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-conc-session\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            java.util.Set<String> ids = java.util.Collections.synchronizedSet(\n                    new java.util.HashSet<>());\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> ids.add(rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A)\n                        .sessionId()));\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            for (Thread w : live) {\n                try {\n                    w.join(60_000);\n                } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                }\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"distinct ids\", 8, ids.size());\n            TestKit.ok(\"no null session\", !ids.contains(null));\n            TestKit.eq(\"all resolve\", 8, rig.sessions.liveSessionCount());\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- rule 7: durable counters\n\n    private static void ledgerPersistence() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"throttle state survives a restart\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-ledger\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n       TestKit.caseOf(\"a racing sibling can only raise the danger level\", () -> {\n            Path dir = TestKit.scratchDir(\"flow-ledger-merge\");\n            Ledger ledger = new     TestKit.caseOf(\"an unwritable ledger never loosens a decision\", () -> {\n            Path dir = TestKit.scratchDir(\"flow-ledger-down\");\n            Path log = dir.resolve(\"throttle.log\");\n rig.throttle.isSourceBlocked(SourceRef.ref(SRC_A)));\n            for (int i = 0; i < victims; i++) {\n                TestKit.ok(\"victim\" + i + \" is not locked\",\n TestKit.caseOf(\"boundary probing is charged to the source budget too\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-src-abuse\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            for ------------------------------------------------------------------ rule 7: atomic\n\n    private static void concurrency() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"a burst cannot exceed the reserved budget\", () -> {\n            // A race that happens to serialise passes for broken code too, so the\n            // assertion is on the exact arithmetic of the reservation rather than on\n            // timing: ALLOWED + THROTTLED == threads and ALLOWED == budget, every run.\n            Ledger ledger = new Ledger(TestKit.scratchDir(\"conc-ledger\").resolve(\"t.log\"));\n            ThrottleManager t = new ThrottleManager(ledger);\n            String acct = Crypto.idRef(\"alice\");\n            String src = SourceRef.ref(SRC_A);\n            int threads = ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES * 6;\n            AtomicInteger allowed = new AtomicInteger();\n            AtomicInteger throttled = new AtomicInteger();\n            ConcurrentLinkedQueue<String> errors = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();\n            CountDownLatch ready = new CountDownLatch(threads);\n            CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> {\n                    ready.countDown();\n                    try {\n                        go.await();\n                    } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    try {\n                        switch (t.beginAttempt(acct, src)) {\n                            case ALLOWED -> allowed.incrementAndGet();\n                            case THROTTLED -> throttled.incrementAndGet();\n                        }\n                    } catch (RuntimeException boom) {\n                        errors.add(boom.toString());\n                    }\n                }, \"burst-\" + i);\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            try {\n                ready.await();\n                go.countDown();\n                for (Thread w : live) {\n                    w.join(60_000);\n                }\n            } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"no worker threw: \" + errors, errors.isEmpty());\n            TestKit.eq(\"every thread got a verdict\", threads, allowed.get() + throttled.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"exactly the budget was reserved\",\n                    ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, allowed.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"the rest were refused\",\n                    threads - ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, throttled.get());\n            TestKit.eq(\"the stored count never overshot\",\n                    ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, t.failureCountFor(acct));\n            TestKit.ok(\"the account ends up blocked\", t.isAccountBlocked(acct));\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"concurrent wrong passwords cannot sneak a grant\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-conc-auth\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            int threads = 4;\n            AtomicInteger granted = new AtomicInteger();\n            CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < threads; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> {\n                    try {\n                        go.await();\n                    } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                        return;\n                    }\n                    if (rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A).isSuccess()) {\n                        granted.incrementAndGet();\n                    }\n                }, \"auth-\" + i);\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            try {\n                go.countDown();\n                for (Thread w : live) {\n                    w.join(120_000);\n                }\n            } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"nobody is authenticated by a race\", 0, granted.get());\n            TestKit.ok(\"the counter stayed within the budget\",\n                    rig.throttle.failureCountFor(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"))\n                            <= ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES);\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"concurrent successes each get a distinct session\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-conc-session\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            java.util.Set<String> ids = java.util.Collections.synchronizedSet(\n                    new java.util.HashSet<>());\n            List<Thread> live = new ArrayList<>();\n            for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {\n                Thread w = new Thread(() -> ids.add(\n                        rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A).sessionId()));\n                live.add(w);\n                w.start();\n            }\n            for (Thread w : live) {\n                try {\n                    w.join(120_000);\n                } catch (InterruptedException gone) {\n                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();\n                }\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"distinct ids\", 8, ids.size());\n            TestKit.ok(\"no null session\", !ids.contains(null));\n            TestKit.eq(\"all resolve\", 8, rig.sessions.liveSessionCount());\n        });\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------- rule 7: durable counters\n\n    private static void ledgerPersistence() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"throttle state survives a restart\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-ledger\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n            }\n            TestKit.ok(\"blocked before the restart\",\n                    rig.throttle.isAccountBlocked(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")));\n            TestKit.ok(\"ledger file exists\", rig.ledger.exists());\n            TestKit.eq(\"ledger mode is private\", \"rw-------\",\n                    TestKit.mode(rig.dir.resolve(\"throttle.log\")));\n            ThrottleManager restarted =\n                    new ThrottleManager(new Ledger(rig.dir.resolve(\"throttle.log\")));\n }\n            Path log = rig.dir.resolve(\"throttle.log\");\n            PrivateFiles.writePrivateAtomic(log,\n                    \"v1|a|garbage line that is not a fresh.beginAttempt(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"), SourceRef.ref(SRC_A));\n            Map<String, Ledger.Counter> after =\n                    ledger.load(now, ThrottleManager.RETENTION_SECONDS);\n directory cannot be replaced by an atomic move\n            ThrottleManager t = new ThrottleManager(new Ledger(log));\n            String acct = Crypto.idRef(\"alice\");\n            int allowed = 0;\n            for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES + 3; i++) {\n                if (t.beginAttempt(acct, SourceRef.ref(SRC_A)) == ThrottleManager.Kind.ALLOWED) {\n                    allowed++;\n                }\n            }\n            TestKit.eq(\"in-memory enforcement held\",\n                    ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES, allowed);\n -------------------------------------------------------------- rule 4: sessions\n\n    private static void sessions() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"session lifetimes\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = private static void csrf() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the csrf pair is single-use and must match\", () -> {\n            SessionManager s = new SessionManager();\n            String token =           TestKit.ok(\"one half missing refused\", !s.consumeCsrfToken(token, null));\n            TestKit.ok(\"both missing refused\", !s.consumeCsrfToken(null, null));\n   }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------- rule 6: comparable work per path\n\n    private static void timings() {\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"every outcome costs the same work\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-timing\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            rig.add(\"carol\", TestKit.PW_CAROL);\n            rig.store.disableAccount(\"carol\");\n            rig.throttle.setTimingControlsForTesting(true, 0);\n            try {\n                Runnable burnFive = () -> {\n                    rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\"));\n                    for (int i = 0; i < ThrottleManager.ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES; i++) {\n                        rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A);\n                    }\n                };\n                List<TimedPath> paths = List.of(\n                        new TimedPath(\"correct\",\n                                () -> rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")),\n                                () -> rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"wrong-password\",\n                                () -> rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")),\n                                () -> rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"unknown-name\",\n                                () -> rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"ghost\")),\n                                () -> rig.login(\"ghost\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"malformed-name\", () -> {\n                        }, () -> rig.login(\"bad name!\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"malformed-secret\", () -> {\n                        }, () -> rig.login(\"alice\", \"x\", SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"throttled\", burnFive,\n                                () -> rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"disabled-account\", () -> {\n                        }, () -> rig.login(\"carol\", TestKit.PW_WRONG, SRC_A)));\n\n                Map<String, Long> median = new java.util.LinkedHashMap<>();\n                for (TimedPath p : paths) {\n                    p.prep().run();\n                    p.call().run();                       // warm up\n                    List<Long> samples = new ArrayList<>();\n                    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n                        p.prep().run();                   // untimed setup\n                        long t0 = System.nanoTime();\n                        p.call().run();                   // one authenticate, timed alone\n                        samples.add((System.nanoTime() - t0) / 1_000_000);\n                    }\n                    java.util.Collections.sort(samples);\n                    median.put(p.name(), samples.get(samples.size() / 2));\n                }\n                long min = Long.MAX_VALUE;\n                long max = 0;\n                for (Map.Entry<String, Long> e : median.entrySet()) {\n                    TestKit.measure(\"path-ms-\" + e.getKey(), String.valueOf(e.getValue()));\n                    min = Math.min(min, e.getValue());\n                    max = Math.max(max, e.getValue());\n                }\n                double spread = (double) max / Math.max(min, 1);\n                TestKit.measure(\"spread-ratio\", String.format(\"%.3f\", spread));\n                TestKit.ok(\"no path is materially cheaper than another (ratio \"\n                        + String.format(\"%.3f\", spread) + \")\", spread < 1.35);\n                // A deleted decoy derivation would show up as one very small column.\n                TestKit.ok(\"the cheapest path still costs a full derivation\", min > 50);\n            } finally {\n                rig.throttle.setTimingControlsForTesting(false, 0);\n            }\n        });\n\n        TestKit.caseOf(\"the padding holds every path up to the floor\", () -> {\n            Rig rig = new Rig(\"flow-timing-floor\");\n            rig.add(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE);\n            long floor = 600_000_000L;  // 600 ms, well above one 100k-iteration derivation\n            rig.throttle.setTimingControlsForTesting(false, floor);\n            TestKit.ok(\"the floor ratcheted up\", rig.throttle.latencyFloorNanos() >= floor);\n            try {\n                List<TimedPath> paths = List.of(\n                        new TimedPath(\"correct\",\n                                () -> rig.throttle.clearAccountForTesting(Crypto.idRef(\"alice\")),\n                                () -> rig.login(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, SRC_A)),\n                        new TimedPath(\"wrong\",\n                                () -> it is\n * never accepted from a caller as proof of anything. What the cookie carries is only a\n * lookup key: {@link #find} validates the wire shape, hashes the value, and requires a\n * live server-side entry that has not expired. No entry, expired entry, wrong shape\n * =&gt; anonymous. A forged or guessed cookie therefore grants exactly nothing, and a\n * dumped map does not yield usable ids because only SHA-256(id) is stored.\n *\n * <p>Both maps are bounded and evict oldest-first, so a client that mints requests\n * cannot grow the heap without limit.\n *\n * <h2>Remaining risk, stated plainly</h2>\n * A session id stolen from a browser (XSS, malware, a shared workstation) is usable by\n * the thief until it expires. Mitigations: {@code HttpOnly} (no script reads it),\n * {@code Secure} + HTTPS-only listener (no network sniffing), {@code SameSite=Strict}\n * (not sent on cross-site requests), 20-minute idle / 8-hour absolute lifetime, and a\n * logout that deletes the server-side entry. Full defence needs per-device key\n * confirmation, which is outside this feature.\n */\npublic final class SessionManager {\n\n    public static final Duration IDLE_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(20);\n    public static final Duration ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofHours(8);\n    public static final Duration CSRF_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofMinutes(15);\n    public static final int MAX_SESSIONS = 10_000;\n    public static final int MAX_PENDING_CSRF = 50_000;\n\n    public static final class Session {\n        public final String username;\n        final long issuedAtEpochSecond;\n        long lastUsedEpochSecond;\n\n        Session(String username, long now) {\n            this.username = username;\n            this.issuedAtEpochSecond = now;\n            this.lastUsedEpochSecond = now;\n        }\n    }\n\n    private final Object monitor = new Object();\n\n    /** Bounded, insertion-ordered so eviction is deterministic. Keyed by SHA-256(id). */\n    private final LinkedHashMap<String, Session> sessions =\n            new LinkedHashMap<>(64, 0.75f, false) {\n                @Override\n                protected boolean removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<String, Session> eldest) {\n                    return size() > MAX_SESSIONS;\n                }\n            };\n\n    private final LinkedHashMap<String, Long> pendingCsrf = new LinkedHashMap<>();\n    private long evictedSessions;\n    private long expiredLookups;\n\n    /** Mint a new session. Only ever called after a verified password match. */\n    public String issue(String username) {\n        String id = Crypto.randomUrlToken(InputPolicy.SESSION_TOKEN_BYTES);\n        long now = AuditClock.epochSecond();\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            int before = sessions.size();\n            sessions.put(Crypto.sha256Hex(id), new Session(username, now));\n            evictedSessions += Math.max(0, before + 1 - MAX_SESSIONS);\n        }\n        return id;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Resolve a cookie value to a live session. Any deviation is a silent\n     * \"not authenticated\" -- there is nothing to leak, because a caller who holds a\n     * valid id is authenticated and one who does not must learn nothing about why.\n     */\n    public Optional<Session> find(String presentedId) {\n        if (!InputPolicy.isSessionToken(presentedId)) {\n            return Optional.empty();\n        }\n        String key = Crypto.sha256Hex(presentedId);\n        long now = AuditClock.epochSecond();\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            Session s = sessions.get(key);\n            if (s == null) {\n                return Optional.empty();\n            }\n            if (now - s.issuedAtEpochSecond > ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT.getSeconds()) {\n                sessions.remove(key);\n                expiredLookups++;\n                return Optional.empty();\n            }\n            if (now - s.lastUsedEpochSecond > IDLE_TIMEOUT.getSeconds()) {\n                sessions.remove(key);\n                expiredLookups++;\n                return Optional.empty();\n            }\n            s.lastUsedEpochSecond = now;\n            return Optional.of(s);\n        }\n    }\n\n    public void logout(String presentedId) {\n        if (!InputPolicy.isSessionToken(presentedId)) {\n            return;\n        }\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            sessions.remove(Crypto.sha256Hex(presentedId));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /** Bind an identity to every live session of that user (used after a password change). */\n    public void revokeAllFor(String username) {\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            Iterator<Map.Entry<String, Session>> it = sessions.entrySet().iterator();\n            while (it.hasNext()) {\n                if (it.next().getValue().username.equals(username)) {\n                    it.remove();\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    public int issueCsrfToken(String cookieValue, String hiddenValue) {\n        long now = AuditClock.epochSecond();\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            pruneCsrfLocked(now);\n            if (pendingCsrf.size() >= MAX_PENDING_CSRF) {\n                Iterator<String> it = pendingCsrf.keySet().iterator();\n                if (it.hasNext()) {\n                    it.next();\n                    it.remove();\n                }\n            }\n            pendingCsrf.put(Crypto.sha256Hex(cookieValue + \"\\n\" + hiddenValue),\n                    now + CSRF_TIMEOUT.getSeconds());\n        }\n        return pendingCsrf.size();\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Consume a CSRF token. Both halves must be present, well-formed, and match each\n     * other and a token we issued; the entry is removed either way so a token cannot be\n     * replayed.\n     */\n    public boolean consumeCsrfToken(String cookieValue, String hiddenValue) {\n        if (!InputPolicy.isCsrfToken(cookieValue) || !InputPolicy.isCsrfToken(hiddenValue)) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (!Crypto.equalConstantTime(cookieValue, hiddenValue)) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        String key = Crypto.sha256Hex(cookieValue + \"\\n\" + hiddenValue);\n        long now = AuditClock.epochSecond();\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            Long until = pendingCsrf.remove(key);\n            return until != null && until > now;\n        }\n    }\n\n    public int purgeExpired() {\n        long now = AuditClock.epochSecond();\n        int removed = 0;\n        synchronized (monitor) {\n            Iterator<Map.Entry<String, Session>> it = sessions.entrySet().iterator();\n            while (it.hasNext()) {\n                Session s = it.next().getValue();\n                if (now - Literal-only parsing also\n * rejects IPv6 scope ids ({@code %eth0}), which would otherwise leak an interface name\n * into a derived value.\n *\n * <p>{@code X-Forwarded-For} is honoured only when the socket peer is inside the\n * configured trusted-proxy set, and then by walking the list right-to-left and stopping\n * at the first address that is not a trusted proxy. That's a genuine functional bug — but is it a *security* bug? Failing to honour XFF means attributing to the socket peer (the proxy). Effect: all clients behind the proxy share one throttle bucket. PEER);\n            cells.put(\"unknown-form-key\", site.post(\"/login\",\n                    \"username=alice&password=\" + TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"&csrf=\" + site.freshCsrf()\n                            + \"&admin=yes\", FORM, null));\n            cells.put(\"duplicate-form-key\", site.post(\"/login\",\n                    \"username=alice&username=bob&password=\" + TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"&csrf=\"\n                            + site.freshCsrf(), FORM, null));\n            cells.put(\"empty-body\", site.post(\"/login\", \"\", FORM, null));\n            cells.put(\"oversized-body\",
