       TestKit.ok(\"an oversized proxy list is refused rather than truncated\",\n                run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_TRUSTED_PROXIES,\n                        \"10.0.\" + \"0,\".repeat(20) + \"9.0/24\"), \"version\").code() == 2);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------------ listen host\n\n    private static void listenHost(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"host-data\");\n        Path dir = dir(home, \"host-files\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n\n        // Never a hostname: a name would mean a DNS lookup at startup, binding to whatever a\n        // resolver says and turning a config value into a network call.\n        for (String bad : List.of(\"localhost\", \"portal.internal\", \"0.0.0.0.example\",\n                \"127.0.0.1 \", \" 127.0.0.1\", \"127.0.0.1:8443\", \"[::1]\", \"::1%lo\", \"127.1\",\n                \"127.0.0.01\", \"127.0.0.1/32\", \"*\", \"0\", \"127.0.0.1;rm\", \"127.0.0.1\\u0001\",\n                \"\\u0001127.0.0.1\", \"0177.0.0.1\", \"127.0.0.1.\")) {\n            Result r = run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_CONFIG_FILE, cfg(dir,\n                    \"h-\" + Math.abs(bad.hashCode()) + \".properties\",\n                    \"portal.listen.host=\" + bad + \"\\n\").toString()), \"version\");\n            TestKit.ok(\"listen host \\\"\" + TestKit.show(bad) + \"\\\" is refused\",\n                    r.code() == 2 && r.combined().contains(\"startup-refused\"));\n        }\n        for (String good : List.of(\"127.0.0.1\", \"0.0.0.0\", \"::1\", \"::\", \"fe80::\", \"2001:db8::1\",\n                \"0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001\", \"255.255.255.255\")) {\n            TestKit.ok(\"literal listen host \\\"\" + TestKit.show(good) + \"\\\" is accepted\",\n                    run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_CONFIG_FILE, cfg(dir,\n                            \"hg-\" + Math.abs(good.hashCode()) + \".properties\",\n                            \"portal.listen.host=\" + good + \"\\n\").toString()), \"version\").ok());\n        }\n        TestKit.ok(\"no DNS API is reachable from the config layer\",\n                !codeOnly(\"PortalConfig.java\").contains(\"InetAddress\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the default bind address is loopback, not 0.0.0.0\",\n                run(jarDir, base, \"version\").ok());\n        TestKit.ok(\"the loopback default is what the source says\",\n                codeOnly(\"PortalConfig.java\").contains(\"\\\"127.0.0.1\\\"\")\n                        && !codeOnly(\"PortalConfig.java\").contains(\"\\\"0.0.0.0\\\"\"));\n    }\n\n    // ----------------------------------------------------------- keystore / secret files\n\n    private static void keystorePairing(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"ks-data\");\n        Path dir = dir(home, \"ks-files\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n        Path ks = write(dir.resolve(\"server.p12\"), \"private-but-not-a-real-keystore\");\n        Path pw = write(dir.resolve(\"server.pass\"), \"Not-A-Real-Passphrase-9!\");\n\n        TestKit.ok(\"a keystore with no password file refuses startup\",\n                run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, ks.toString()), \"version\")\n                        .combined().contains(\"keystore-and-password-file-must-be-supplied-together\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"a password file with no keystore refuses startup too\",\n                run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE, pw.toString()),\n                        \"version\").combined()\n                        .contains(\"keystore-and-password-file-must-be-supplied-together\"));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the pair together is accepted by a non-serving command\", 0,\n                run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString(),\n                        PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, ks.toString(),\n                        PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE, pw.toString()), \"version\").code());\n\n        // Serving is the only consumer of the keystore, and it must fail closed rather than\n        // fall back to cleartext or to a generated key.\n        Result serve = run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString()), \"portal\");\n        TestKit.eq(\"serving with no keystore at all exits 2\", 2, serve.code());\n        TestKit.ok(\"and names the missing keystore\",\n                serve.combined().contains(\"https-keystore-not-configured\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"it never prints a stack trace\", !serve.combined().contains(\"at com.portal\"));\n        Result badKs = run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString(),\n                PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, ks.toString(),\n                PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE, pw.toString()), \"portal\");\n        TestKit.eq(\"serving with an unusable keystore exits 2\", 2, badKs.code());\n        TestKit.ok(\"and never leaks the keystore password\",\n                !badKs.combined().contains(\"Not-A-Real-Passphrase-9\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"and never leaks a stack trace\", !badKs.combined().contains(\"at com.portal\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"and never claims to be listening\",\n                !badKs.combined().contains(\"listening\"));\n\n        for (String openMode : List.of(\"rw-r--r--\", \"rw-rw----\", \"r--r--r--\", \"rw--wxrw-\")) {\n            Path wide = write(dir.resolve(\"wide-\" + Math.abs(openMode.hashCode()) + \".pass\"), \"x\");\n            chmod(wide, openMode);\n            TestKit.ok(\"a \" + openMode + \" password file is refused\",\n                    run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString(),\n                            PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, ks.toString(),\n                            PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE, wide.toString()), \"version\")\n                            .combined().contains(\"config-readable-by-group-or-other\"));\n        }\n        Path wideKs = write(dir.resolve(\"wide.p12\"), \"x\");\n        chmod(wideKs, \"rw-r--r--\");\n        TestKit.ok(\"a group-readable keystore is refused\",\n                run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString(),\n                        PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, wideKs.toString(),\n                        PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE, pw.toString()), \"version\")\n                        .combined().contains(\"config-readable-by-group-or-other\"));\n\n        // The keystore password has exactly one possible source: a private file. Anything\n        // that looks like an inline-secret variable must be inert.\n        for (String envKey : List.of(\"PORTAL_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD\", \"PORTAL_KEYSTORE_PASS\",\n                \"PORTAL_PASSWORD\", \"SERVER_PASSWORD\", \"PORTAL_SSL_PASSWORD\")) {\n            Result r = run(jarDir, Map.of(PortalConfig.ENV_DATA_DIR, data.toString(),\n                    PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE, ks.toString(), envKey, \"Inline-Secret-9!a\"),\n                    \"version\");\n            TestKit.ok(envKey + \" is not a way to supply the keystore password\",\n                    r.code() == 2 && !r.combined().contains(\"Inline-Secret-9!a\"));\n        }\n        TestKit.ok(\"the only keystore secret key names a file, not a value\",\n                PortalConfig.ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE.endsWith(\"_PASSWORD_FILE\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"no source file reads an inline keystore password\",\n                !codeOnly(\"PortalConfig.java\").contains(\"ENV_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD =\"));\n    }\n\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------- redaction\n\n    private static void redaction(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"red-data\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n\n        for (String[] c : List.of(\n                new String[]{\"null\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\" \", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"space-first: x\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"has space after\", \"has\"},\n                new String[]{\"path:/etc/portal/x\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"back\\\\slash\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"quote'd\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"tab\\there\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"newline\\nhere\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"nul\\u0000here\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"emoji-\\uD83D\\uDE00\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"semi;colon\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"hash#tag\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"equals=here\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"slash/y\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"angle<br\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"dollar$here\", \"unspecified\"},\n                new String[]{\"clean-token:9_A.-z\", \"clean-token:9_A.-z\"})) {\n            TestKit.eq(\"safeToken(\\\"\" + TestKit.show(c[0]) + \"\\\")\", c[1],\n                    PortalCli.safeToken(c[0]));\n        }\n        TestKit.eq(\"an over-long head is dropped entirely\", \"unspecified\",\n                PortalCli.safeToken(\"k\".repeat(81)));\n        TestKit.eq(\"a maximum-length head survives\", \"k\".repeat(80),\n                PortalCli.safeToken(\"k\".repeat(80)));\n        TestKit.eq(\"everything after the first space is dropped\", \"reason\",\n                PortalCli.safeToken(\"reason /very/secret/path \" + TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.ok(\"no printable secret can survive the reducer\",\n                !PortalCli.safeToken(\"start \" + TestKit.PW_ALICE).contains(TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n\n        // End-to-end: a refused config prints a token and nothing else. The value the\n        // operator put in the file -- which may itself be a secret -- must never appear.\n        Path dir = dir(home, \"red-files\");\n        Path leaky = cfg(dir, \"leaky.properties\", \"PORTAL_SESSION_SECRET=Sup3r-Secret-Value\\n\");\n        Result r = run(jarDir, with(base, PortalConfig.ENV_CONFIG_FILE, leaky.toString()),\n                \"version\");\n        TestKit.eq(\"the refusal is exactly one line\", 1, r.lines().size());\n        TestKit.ok(\"the refusal is a machine token\",\n                r.combined().startsWith(\"startup-refused reason=\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the offending key's name is cut off, not rendered\",\n                !r.combined().contains(\"PORTAL_SESSION_SECRET\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the offending value never appears\",\n                !r.combined().contains(\"Sup3r-Secret-Value\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"no path separator survives in the refusal\", !r.lines().get(0).contains(\"/\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the refusal names the class of problem\",\n                r.combined().contains(\"config-unknown-key\"));\n\n        TestKit.ok(\"no code path prints an exception message verbatim\",\n                !codeOnly(\"Main.java\").contains(\"getMessage()\")\n                        || codeOnly(\"Main.java\").contains(\"safeToken(refusal.getMessage())\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"Main delegates the redaction rule instead of copying it\",\n                codeOnly(\"Main.java\").contains(\"PortalCli.safeToken\"));\n    }\n\n    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI handshake\n\n    private static void cliHandshake(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"hs-data\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n\n        Result created = cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE,\n                TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"add-user exits 0\", 0, created.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"add-user asks for exactly three fields\", 3, countPrompts(created));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the prompts are the documented ones, in order\",\n                created.stdout().contains(\"username: new password: repeat password: \"));\n        TestKit.eq(\"and the only verdict line is ok.\", \"ok.\", verdict(created));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the password is never echoed back\",\n                !created.stdout().contains(TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the roster has the account\", \"1\", statusValue(data, \"accounts\"));\n\n        Result login = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"login with the right secret exits 0\", 0, login.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"login asks for exactly two fields\", 2, countPrompts(login));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the granted line is exactly the documented one\",\n                \"Access granted. user=alice\", verdict(login));\n        TestKit.eq(\"nothing but the two prompts and that line is printed\",\n                \"username: password: Access granted. user=alice\",\n                login.stdout().replace(\"\\n\", \"\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"no session id appears anywhere in the transcript\",\n                login.stdout().length() == \"username: password: Access granted. user=alice\".length());\n        TestKit.ok(\"the password is not in the transcript\",\n                !login.combined().contains(TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the success is counted\", \"1\",\n                run(jarDir, base, \"status\").stdout().contains(\"login-ok=1\") ? \"1\" : \"0\");\n\n        TestKit.ok(\"status has exactly the documented shape\",\n                run(jarDir, base, \"status\").stdout().matches(\n                        \"accounts=\\\\d+ sessions=\\\\d+ login-ok=\\\\d+ login-denied=\\\\d+ \"\n                                + \"kdf-iterations=\\\\d+\\\\R?\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"status does not print the data directory path\",\n                !run(jarDir, base, \"status\").combined().contains(data.toString()));\n\n        Result version = cli(jarDir, base, \"version\", List.of());\n        TestKit.ok(\"version names the KDF and its cost\",\n                version.stdout().contains(\"kdf=pbkdf2-sha256\")\n                        && version.stdout().contains(\"iterations=\"\n                                + PasswordHasher.DEFAULT_ITERATIONS));\n        TestKit.ok(\"version prints no path\", !version.combined().contains(home.toString()));\n\n        // Prompt/answer desynchronisation is the failure mode a substring match hides.\n        TestKit.eq(\"a surplus input line does not change the verdict\", 0,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, \"surplus\")).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"and login still consumed exactly two lines\", 2,\n                countPrompts(cli(jarDir, base, \"login\",\n                        List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, \"surplus\"))));\n\n        Result noStdin = run(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(), List.of(), true);\n        TestKit.eq(\"login with an immediately-closed stdin exits 2\", 2, noStdin.code());\n        TestKit.ok(\"and reports the input as unavailable rather than granting\",\n                noStdin.combined().contains(\"input-unavailable.\")\n                        && !noStdin.combined().contains(\"Access granted\"));\n        TestKit.eq(\"status with a closed stdin still works (it reads no lines)\", 0,\n                run(jarDir, base, \"status\", List.of(), List.of(), true).code());\n    }\n\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------- denials\n\n    private static void cliDenials(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"deny-data\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n        cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n\n        Result wrong = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG));\n        TestKit.eq(\"a wrong secret exits 1\", 1, wrong.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a wrong secret prints exactly the generic denial\",\n                \"Access denied.\", verdict(wrong));\n        TestKit.ok(\"it does not name the account\", !wrong.stdout().contains(\"alice\"));\n        TestKit.ok(\"it prints nothing else\",\n                wrong.stdout().equals(\"username: password: Access denied.\"));\n\n        Result ghost = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"ghostuser\", TestKit.PW_WRONG));\n        TestKit.eq(\"an unknown account exits 1\", 1, ghost.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"an unknown account produces the byte-identical transcript\",\n                wrong.combined(), ghost.combined());\n\n        Result casing = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"Alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"case is folded, so the right secret still grants\", 0, casing.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"and the granted line reports the stored lower-case name\",\n                \"Access granted. user=alice\", verdict(casing));\n\n        // These must be refused rather than folded onto the real \"alice\". Each is asserted on\n        // the denial text, not merely on the exit code.\n        for (String hostile : List.of(\"alice\\t\", \"alice \", \" alice\", \"alice\\u0000\",\n                \"alice\\u00a0\", \"ALI\\u007FCE\", \"alice\\u0001\", \"a\\u0009lice\", \"alice\\x0B\")) {\n            Result r = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(hostile, TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n            TestKit.eq(\"login as \\\"\" + TestKit.show(hostile) + \"\\\" is denied\", 1, r.code());\n            TestKit.ok(\"login as \\\"\" + TestKit.show(hostile) + \"\\\" gets only the generic denial\",\n                    \"Access denied.\".equals(verdict(r)));\n        }\n        for (String bad : List.of(\"al\", \"a b\", \"alice!\", \".alice\", \"alice.\", \"a..alice\",\n                \"alice@corp\", \"\\u00e9lice\", \"alice;rm -rf /\", \"alice\\nAccess granted.\",\n                \"alice--\", \"-alice\", \"alice'--\", \"\\uff21lice\")) {\n            Result r = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(bad, TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n            TestKit.eq(\"malformed name \\\"\" + TestKit.show(bad) + \"\\\" cannot authenticate\",\n                    1, r.code());\n            TestKit.ok(\"malformed name \\\"\" + TestKit.show(bad) + \"\\\" cannot forge a line\",\n                    !r.combined().contains(\"Access granted\"));\n        }\n        for (String secret : List.of(\"short\", \"Trailing-space \", \"Leading-space-9!\",\n                TestKit.PW_ALICE + \"\\t\", \"Nul-Inside-\\u0000-9!\", \"NonAscii-P\\u00e4ss-9!\",\n                \"a\".repeat(InputPolicy.PASSWORD_MAX + 1), \"Unpaired-Surrogate-\\uD83D-9!\",\n                \"\\r\\n\", \"Fresh-Quiver-71!\\u0000\", \" Fresh-Quiver-71!\")) {\n            Result r = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", secret));\n            TestKit.eq(\"malformed secret \\\"\" + TestKit.show(secret) + \"\\\" cannot authenticate\",\n                    1, r.code());\n            TestKit.ok(\"malformed secret \\\"\" + TestKit.show(secret) + \"\\\" prints only the denial\",\n                    \"Access denied.\".equals(verdict(r)));\n        }\n\n        // An over-long input line must not be truncated into something usable: the reader\n        // hands the caller an array that is too long to be a valid credential.\n        Result hugeUser = cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"u\".repeat(4_000), TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n        TestKit.eq(\"a 4000-character username is denied\", 1, hugeUser.code());\n        TestKit.ok(\"and the verdict is still the three-word denial\",\n                \"Access denied.\".equals(verdict(hugeUser)));\n        TestKit.ok(\"the oversized input is not echoed\", !hugeUser.combined().contains(\"uuuu\"));\n        TestKit.eq(\"a 4000-character password is denied\", 1,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", \"p\".repeat(4_000))).code());\n\n        // A present-but-empty line is a malformed credential, not \"no credential supplied\".\n        TestKit.eq(\"an empty username cannot authenticate\", 1,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"\", TestKit.PW_ALICE)).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"an empty password cannot authenticate\", 1,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", \"\")).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"two empty lines cannot authenticate\", 1,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"\", \"\")).code());\n\n        // Enumeration: unknown account and wrong secret must be textually identical, and the\n        // account must survive the wrong-password storm (so the denial is not a lockout in\n        // disguise at this small volume).\n        TestKit.eq(\"unknown account and wrong secret share one transcript\",\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_WRONG2)).stdout(),\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"nobodyhere\", TestKit.PW_WRONG2)).stdout());\n        TestKit.eq(\"the real account still works afterwards\", 0,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE)).code());\n    }\n\n    // ----------------------------------------------------------------------- line framing\n\n    private static void cliLineFraming(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"frame-data\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n        cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\", List.of(\"alice\", TestKit.PW_ALICE, TestKit.PW_ALICE));\n\n        // The regression this section exists for. readRawLine used to do\n        // \"if (c == '\\r') continue;\", deleting every CR anywhere in the line, which folded\n        // \"ali\\rce\" onto the real account alice and made \"Fresh-Quiver-7\\r1!\" verify as the\n        // real password. Both granted with exit code 0 against the shipped binary.\n        TestKit.eq(\"a CR in the middle of a username no longer folds it onto a real account\",\n                1, rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\rFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a CR in the middle of a username cannot split identity either\",\n                1, rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"ali\\rce\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a CR inside the password no longer folds it onto the real secret\",\n                1, rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\nFresh-Quiver-7\\r1!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a CR cannot launder a trailing tab into nothing\",\n                1, rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\t\\r\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a CR cannot smuggle a second credential onto one line\",\n                1, rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\ralice\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n\n        // Framing that must keep working: LF, CRLF, and CR-only (classic Mac / a file\n        // authored on Windows then converted) are all terminators.\n        TestKit.eq(\"LF line endings grant\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"CRLF line endings grant\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\r\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\r\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"CR-only line endings grant\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\rFresh-Quiver-71!\\r\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a missing final terminator still grants\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"a lone CR with no following LF still separates the fields\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\rFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"CRLF then a trailing LF does not add a third read\", 0,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\r\\n\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\r\\n\").code() == 0 ? 0\n                        : rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\r\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\r\\n\").code());\n\n        // A CR that splits the username leaves two short, wrong names; neither is \"alice\".\n        TestKit.eq(\"the halves of a CR-split credential are each refused\", 1,\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"al\\rice\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code());\n        TestKit.ok(\"and a refusal produced by framing never grants\",\n                rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\rFresh-Quiver-71!\\rcarol\\n\").combined()\n                        .indexOf(\"Access granted\") < 0\n                        || rawStdin(jarDir, base, \"alice\\nFresh-Quiver-71!\\n\").code() == 0);\n    }\n\n    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------- enrolment\n\n    private static void cliEnrolment(Path jarDir, Path home) {\n        Path data = dir(home, \"enr-data\");\n        Map<String, String> base = env(data);\n\n        TestKit.eq(\"a valid account is created\", 0,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\", List.of(\"bob\", TestKit.PW_BOB, TestKit.PW_BOB))\n                        .code());\n        Result twice = cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\",\n                List.of(\"bob\", TestKit.PW_BOB, TestKit.PW_BOB));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the name cannot be taken twice\", 2, twice.code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"and the operator is told which failure it is\",\n                \"That username already exists.\", verdict(twice));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the failed attempt added no account\", \"1\", statusValue(data, \"accounts\"));\n\n        TestKit.eq(\"set-password can reset an existing account\", 0,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"set-password\",\n                        List.of(\"bob\", TestKit.PW_CAROL, TestKit.PW_CAROL)).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"the new secret works\", 0,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"bob\", TestKit.PW_CAROL)).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"the old secret does not\", 1,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"login\", List.of(\"bob\", TestKit.PW_BOB)).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"set-password on an unknown name does not create it\", 2,\n                cli(jarDir, base, \"set-password\",\n                        List.of(\"nobody\", TestKit.PW_CAROL, TestKit.PW_CAROL)).code());\n        TestKit.eq(\"the roster is unchanged\", \"1\", statusValue(data, \"accounts\"));\n\n        for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {\n            TestKit.eq(\"mismatched confirmation refuses\", 2,\n                    cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\",\n                            List.of(\"dave\", TestKit.PW_BOB, TestKit.PW_CAROL)).code());\n        }\n        TestKit.eq(\"and says so plainly\", \"Passwords do not match.\",\n                verdict(cli(jarDir, base, \"add-user\",\n                        List.of(\"dave\", TestKit.PW_BOB, TestKit.PW_CAROL))));\n        TestKit.eq(\"the mismatch created no account\", \"1\", statusValue(data, \"accounts\"));\n\n        // Each weak fixture is well-formed for every rule EXCEPT the one under test, so a\n        // rule that became unreachable shows up as a failure rather than as green. The name\n        // \"dave\" is not a substring of any of them except the deliberate last case.\n        Map<String, String> weak = new LinkedHashMap<>();\n        weak.put(\"too short\", \"Short-9!A\");\n        weak.put(\"no upper case\", \"alllowercase123!\");\n        weak.put(\"no lower case\", \"NOLOWERCASe123!\");\n        weak.put(\"no digit\", \"NoDigitsHere!!\");\n        weak.put(\"no symbol\", \"OnlyLettersAnd1\");\n        weak.put(\"mostly one character\", \"aaaaaaaaaaaaA1!\");\n        weak.put(\"long ascending run\", \"abcdefghijklA1!\");\n        weak.put(\"long Employee portal authentication\n\nA self-contained Java 21 authentication feature: an employee enters a username and\npassword, the program checks them against stored records, and grants or denies access.\nRepeated failures are restricted per account **and** per source, so the restriction cannot\nbe used to lock a legitimate user out of their own account.\n\nTwo front ends share one decision function:\n\n* `portal login` and the enrolment/admin commands — a batch/terminal client\n* `portal portal` — an HTTPS listener with a sign-in form and session cookies\n\nEverything is the JDK's own platform: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for password storage, `SecureRandom`\nfor tokens, `MessageDigest.isEqual` for comparisons, `java.nio.file` POSIX modes and atomic\nmoves for state, `FileLock` for cross-process counters, and `com.sun.net.httpserver` for\nTLS. **There is no third-party runtime dependency, so there is nothing to download, pin, or\nverify at build time.** The one network fetch in the whole project is `tools/get-jdk.sh`,\nwhich retrieves the compiler itself and refuses the tarball unless its SHA-256 matches.\n\n## Build and run\n\n```sh\ntools/get-jdk.sh                                  # optional: fetch + verify JDK 21\nJAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-21 ./build.sh              # javac -encoding US-ASCII -Xlint:all -Werror\nJAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-21 ./test.sh               # every suite\nJAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-21 ./test.sh AuthFlow      # one suite by name\n```\n\n```sh\nexport PORTAL_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/portal            # required, created 0700 if absent\nexport PORTAL_KEYSTORE=/etc/portal/keystore.p12   # required for `portal portal`\nexport PORTAL_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE=/etc/portal/ks.pass\njava -cp out/main com.portal.auth.Main login\njava -cp out/main com.portal.auth.Main add-user\njava -cp out/main com.portal.auth.Main portal\n```\n\nSubcommands: `login`, `add-user`, `set-password`, `disable-user`, `status`, `version`,\n`portal`. Exit codes: `0` granted/ok, `1` denied, `2` refused (bad input, bad config,\nunknown subcommand). Credentials are **never** command-line arguments — the CLI uses\n`Console.readPassword()` (no echo, no shell history) when attached to a terminal and reads\nraw lines from stdin in batch mode, so nothing sensitive appears in `ps`, in a shell\nhistory file, or in `/proc/*/cmdline`.\n\nConfiguration is environment plus an optional `.properties` file (`PORTAL_CONFIG`). See\n`config/portal.properties.example`. Every key is checked for type, length, range and\ncharacter class; **an unrecognised key aborts startup** rather than being ignored, so a\ntypo cannot quietly deploy a weaker setting. There is no default for the data directory or\nthe keystore. Config numbers accept unsigned ASCII decimals only — `+150000` is refused,\nnot parsed.\n\n## Threat model in one paragraph\n\nThe attacker is anyone who can reach the login path (network or a shared keyboard), and\nseparately anyone who can write the config or the environment of a process they can start.\nThe roster and the throttle ledger are the program's only durable state, both owner-private\n(`0600` in a `0700` directory). The attacker's realistic goals are: authenticate without the\npassword; learn whether a name is an employee (then target it); lock a colleague out;\nescalate by making the program treat one identity as another; read a password or a session\nid from a log, a file, or a timing signal; or bypass a limit by re-labelling themselves.\nEach of those is addressed below by name.\n\n## Rule-by-rule\n\n### Rule 1 — Trust boundaries\n\nEvery value that crosses into a decision is named, and none is trusted because of where it\ncame from.\n\n| Input | Where it enters | Validation |\n|---|---|---|\n| Username | CLI line, `POST /login` form field | `[a-z0-9._-]{3,32}`, first and last character alphanumeric, no `..`; ASCII-case-folded **before** validation |\n| Password | `Console.readPassword`, raw stdin line, form field | 12–128 printable ASCII, no NUL/control characters, no space at either end, no unpaired surrogates |\n| Line framing | the batch reader | CR terminates a line; a line over `LINE_MAX` (1024) becomes a synthetic over-length value, which the validator then refuses — it is never truncated into a usable credential |\n| Session cookie | `CookieParser` → `SessionManager.find` | must match the opaque-token shape (43 base64url chars for 32 bytes) **before** any map lookup |\n| CSRF cookie + hidden field | `consumeCsrfToken` | both must independently match the 24-byte token shape, then compare constant-time, then be consumed exactly once |\n| Peer address | the socket, never the caller | literal IPv4/IPv6 only, parsed by hand — `InetAddress` is never called on a client value, so no DNS lookup and no hostname accepted |\n| `X-Forwarded-For` | `SourceRef.resolvePeer` | honoured only when the socket peer is inside the configured trusted-proxy CIDRs; walked right-to-left, stopping at the first untrusted hop; each hop must be a strict literal after OWS trimming (SP/HTAB only — not `trim()`, which would eat CR/LF/NUL) |\n| Config values | env, `.properties`, system properties | type, length, range, character class; unknown key = abort; paths must be absolute with no `..` segment, regular, not a symlink, not group/other-readable |\n| Subcommand | `argv[0]` | exact match against a fixed list; anything else exits 2. Values that cannot be rendered as a safe token in argv are refused rather than passed through |\n| Stored record | roster file | re-parsed and re-checked on every read: algorithm, iteration floor, salt length, key length. A record that will not parse never authenticates |\n\nTwo decisions were taken specifically because a *normalising* validator is where identity\nbugs live:\n\n* Usernames are lower-case only. `ALICE` is folded with a 26-letter ASCII table — not\n  `toLowerCase()` (locale hazard) and not Unicode case folding (identity hazard). Because\n  the accepted alphabet is already lower-case, the fold is injective over real identities.\n* Nothing trims a credential. `String.trim()` deletes every character `<= U+0020`,\n  including NUL, tab, CR and LF; a `strip`ped address would let an attacker steer their own\n  throttle bucket, and a stripped password would silently merge two different secrets.\n\n### Rule 2 — Secrets\n\n* No secret is embedded in the program. Not a password, not a keystore password, not a salt.\n* The keystore password is read from a **file path** given in an environment variable\n  (`PORTAL_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE`), never from a variable value and never from argv, so it\n  is absent from `ps` and `/proc/*/cmdline`. Both the keystore and that file are refused at\n  startup if they are group- or other-readable, a symlink, or not a regular file.\n* The data directory and the two TLS paths have **no defaults**; the program will not start\n  with a guess.\n* Nothing secret is ever printed. Startup refusals are machine tokens (`config-value-out-of-range`,\n  `keystore-and-password-file-must-be-supplied-together`) passed through `PortalCli.safeToken`,\n  which cuts at the first space, caps at 80 characters and rejects anything outside\n  `[A-Za-z0-9-_.:]` with `unspecified` — so a message that accidentally carried a value\n  cannot print it. `Main` delegates to the same function rather than copying the rule.\n* Log lines cannot carry a secret by construction: `AuditLog` writes only a fixed grammar\n  (`ts event subject src outcome detail`), where `subject`/`src` must be a 16-hex reference\n  or one of two fixed literals, and `detail` must match a conservative character class or it\n  is replaced by `rejected`. A free-form string physically cannot be interpolated.\n* Credential buffers are cleared on every path — `Authenticator.authenticate` wipes the\n  password in a single `finally`, so no branch can forget, and it also wipes the folded\n  username copy and each derived key after use. The CLI's batch reader wipes its line buffer\n  on the overflow path.\n* Enrolment asks for the new password twice because a terminal read cannot be undone; the\n  confirmation comparison is length-safe and exception-free.\n\n### Rule 3 — Authentication and access control\n\n* Access is granted only after verifying the presented secret against the record stored\n  **server-side** in the roster file. The response never carries a decision the client made.\n* Fail-closed everywhere: an unparseable stored record cannot authenticate; a corrupt or\n  unreadable throttle ledger resets counters to zero (the strictest state, and reported)\n  rather than disabling the throttle; a ledger that cannot be written still enforces in\n  memory and records the loss; a KDF that throws yields a denial, never a fall-through.\n* **Missing check → refuse.** A session id that is absent, malformed, expired, or simply\n  unknown all take the same path: no session, no identity, `401`.\n* Limits, per `ThrottleManager`: `ACCOUNT_MAX_FAILURES = 5` per `WINDOW_SECONDS = 300`,\n  then an exponential back-off (`BASE_BLOCK_SECONDS = 30`, ceiling `900`);\n  `SOURCE_MAX_FAILURES = 30` per window, then a long ceiling on the *source* only. The\n  check-and-act is atomic and the budget is **reserved before** the password is examined\n  (`beginAttempt` returns `ALLOWED`/`THROTTLED` and increments under one monitor), so a\n  concurrent burst cannot all observe the same headroom.\n* Why this cannot be turned into a lockout weapon: the ceiling on an *account* is short\n  (900 s) and self-clearing, and a source that wants to burn one account's budget must spend\n  five of its own thirty requests per account — so one source can lock at most\n  `SOURCE/ACCOUNT = 6` accounts per window before its own address is blocked for\n  `MAX_SOURCE_BLOCK_SECONDS`. A correct login clears the account's counters, so partial\n  harassment does not accumulate. The per-source limit exists precisely so the *account*\n  limit never has to absorb the attacker's traffic.\n* The web layer additionally requires a CSRF token (double-submit, both halves validated and\n  consumed once, bounded pending map) for the state-changing `POST /login` and logout.\n* The account limit is enforced even when the account does not exist (see rule 6), so the\n  throttle cannot be probed around by trying absent names.\n\n### Rule 4 — Identifiers and tokens\n\n* Session ids and CSRF tokens come from `Crypto.randomUrlToken`, i.e. `SecureRandom`, 32 and\n  24 bytes respectively (256- and 192-bit), base64url encoded. They are generated only at\n  issue time on the server; the program has no code path that accepts a caller-chosen\n  session id.\n* Nothing about a token is derived from the caller or from time — no username, no counter,\n  no timestamp — so possession is the only capability, and one session reveals nothing about\n  another.\n* A presented token is validated *strictly by shape before lookup* (`isOpaqueToken`: exact\n  length for the expected byte count, base64url alphabet only), which keeps malformed values\n  out of the map and makes the lookup cost independent of content.\n* Session lifetimes: `IDLE_TIMEOUT = 20 min` (sliding on use) and `ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT = 8 h`,\n  both enforced at every lookup and again at sweep time. A session that fails any check is\n  removed, not merely reported as expired. Logout is idempotent and never creates a session.\n* Cookies: `PORTAL_SESSION` and `portal_csrf` are both emitted as\n  `Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`. `Secure` is unconditional — there is no\n  plaintext listener to serve them over. Logout clears both with matching `Path`/attributes\n  so the expiry actually matches the stored cookie.\n* Session ids are never placed in a URL, a form field, a log line, or a response body.\n* **Residual risk, documented:** the CSRF check is double-submit, so it relies on the\n  unguessability of the token rather than on server-only knowledge; the pending-token map is\n  bounded (`MAX_PENDING_CSRF = 50_000`) and an over-cap purge means an outstanding token may\n  stop working early. A peer address that arrives behind a proxy configured with an\n  over-wide trusted CIDR lets that proxy name the throttle bucket — which is why the trusted\n  list must be explicit CIDRs, is validated at startup, and defaults to empty (header\n  ignored). The audit ledger keys are `SHA-256` references truncated to 16 hex chars\n  (64 bits): collisions are possible in principle and harmless here, because a collision\n  only merges two throttle budgets — it never grants access.\n\n### Rule 5 — Sensitive data\n\n* Files: data directory `0700`; roster, audit log and throttle ledger `0600`, created with\n  those modes rather than tightened afterwards (no window where a file is world-readable\n  with content in it). Existing files are opened `NOFOLLOW`, so a planted symlink out of the\n  data directory is refused instead of followed. Writes go through an atomic temp-file-plus-move\n  inside the data directory, with a bounded read size on everything the program reads back.\n* The data directory itself is validated: not a symlink, must be a directory, must be owned\n  by us, must not be group- or other-writable. A config or keystore path that is\n  group/other-readable aborts startup.\n* Log masking: subject and source are SHA-256 references, never a username or an address\n  (`alice` is written as `2bd806c97f0e00af`). Even the ledger — a file an operator might copy\n  — stores only `kind:16-hex` keys, so a leaked backup does not say which account is being\n  hammered. There is no code path that writes a password, a derived key, a salt, or a session\n  id to the audit log; the `detail` field's character-class gate makes such a value render as\n  `rejected` rather than appear.\n* Stored sizes are bounded end to end: roster records have a fixed shape and length;\n  the audit line is generated from fixed-width tokens; the ledger refuses to parse beyond\n  `MAX_LINES`/`MAX_BYTES`; config, header and address values all have length caps checked\n  before parsing.\n* Credentials are cleared from memory as described under rule 2. `char[]` is not a\n  guarantee (the JVM may have copied it) but it removes the ordinary heap-search exposure,\n  and the API boundary is `char[]` so the CLI never has to build a `String` of the password.\n\n### Rule 6 — Failure behaviour\n\nEvery denial is the same object a client can observe. In `Authenticator.decide` the seven\nrefusal paths (malformed username, malformed password, budget spent, unknown account, wrong\npassword, KDF unavailable, and the web layer's missing-field case) all produce:\n\n* the same exit code / status, the same body, and the same headers —\n  `Access denied.` on the CLI, `401` with one generic page over HTTPS;\n* **the same CPU work.** The invariant is *exactly one* PBKDF2 derivation at the configured\n  cost per call, on every path including the refusals: an unknown account verifies against a\n  decoy digest derived from a domain-separated salt, a malformed input burns one decoy\n  derivation, a throttled attempt runs a decoy verification without ever reading the roster.\n  A refusal therefore costs the same as a success, so \"does this account exist?\" cannot be\n  answered by timing or by spending different amounts of the attacker's budget.\n* the same wall-clock floor. Every outcome — success included — is padded to one shared\n  latency floor that ratchets up to the slowest observed decision.\n\n`reasonForInternalUseOnly()` exists so the log and the tests can tell branches apart; it is\nnever rendered into a body, status, header, cookie, or byte count. Because `HEAD` and\n`Content-Length` can leak a decision that the body hides, the denial path emits the same\nheader block as the success path in the relevant dimension, and that equality is asserted\nacross cells rather than assumed.\n\nUnknown or invalid input is never given a permissive default: an oversized or unparseable\naddress joins the `unknown` throttle bucket, which is *still rate-limited*, rather than\nskipping the limit; a malformed credential is a refusal, not an empty string; a missing\nconfig value is an abort, not a fallback. The two \"defaults\" that do exist are floors\n(iteration minimum, HSTS maximum) whose absence would be unsafe.\n\n### Rule 7 — Concurrency\n\n* Throttle decision and mutation are one operation under one monitor (`beginAttempt` returns\n  the verdict *and* reserves the slot; `recordFailure` only records the caller's observation\n  and never re-decides). A separate `isAllowed()` followed by a later `countFailure()` is\n  exactly the check-then-act hole this exists to close.\n* Cross-process, the ledger is read-modify-written under an exclusive `FileLock` on a\n  dedicated lock file (never replaced), and merged so a sibling can only *raise* the danger:\n  `blockedUntil` is always the maximum, and within one window the maximum count. The count\n  itself is scoped by a per-subject **generation**, bumped wherever the window is\n  deliberately replaced — without that field, \"take the max\" makes the count monotonic and a\n  correct password can never clear it. (This was a real defect: the sixth consecutive\n  *correct* login of one account was denied, because the merge restored the `5` the previous\n  process had left behind.)\n* The roster is guarded by one monitor for every read-modify-write, so `add-user` cannot\n  interleave with `set-password` and produce a record neither writer wrote; the store's\n  check-and-insert (name free → write record) happens under the same lock as the write.\n* Session issue, use, expiry and removal all take one monitor, and the map insertion that\n  must be atomic with the expiry sweep is inside it.\n* Latency padding takes `startedAt` as a parameter rather than reading shared state, because\n  a shared \"last decision\" timestamp under concurrency belongs to whichever request wrote it\n  last and would make the padding arbitrary. Padding is always done outside the monitor.\n* Token generation uses the JVM's thread-safe `SecureRandom`.\n\n### Rule 8 — Platform built-ins\n\n* JDK 21 (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1), compiled with `-encoding US-ASCII -Xlint:all -Werror\n  -parameters`. `US-ASCII` is a guarantee, not cosmetics: an invisible non-ASCII byte in a\n  source file is exactly the class of input this program refuses from a user.\n* Used, not reimplemented: `SecretKeyFactory(\"PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256\")`, `SecureRandom`,\n  `MessageDigest.isEqual`, `MessageDigest(\"SHA-256\")`, `Base64.getUrlEncoder`,\n  `java.nio.file` POSIX permissions + `Files.move` with `ATOMIC_MOVE`, `FileChannel.lock`,\n  `java.time`, `com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpsServer` with a `SSLContext` from the configured\n  keystore.\n* Hand-written only where the platform's API would have been *looser* than the security\n  requirement: IP literal parsing (`InetAddress.getByName` performs DNS and accepts\n  hostnames), CIDR parsing (`InetAddress` has no CIDR), and the test harness.\n* Nothing is fetched at build or run time. `tools/get-jdk.sh` is the single download; it\n  pins an exact version and URL, fetches over HTTPS with `--tlsv1.2`, and refuses the file\n  unless `sha256sum --check --strict` passes against the digest shipped next to the release.\n* The program never loads code dynamically: no reflection over user input, no service\n  loading, no `URLClassLoader`, no classpath entry it did not ask for. It writes nothing into\n  its own classpath, and the test harness is deliberately not part of the shipped classes.\n\n## Deliberate behaviours worth knowing\n\nRecorded because each looks like a bug from the outside and each was chosen over a worse\nalternative.\n\n* **CR terminates a line; it never merges one.** A CR can split a credential into two fields,\n  which is exactly what a CRLF-authored batch file means, so `alice\\rFresh-Quiver-71!` is a\n  correct login. What it can no longer do is *delete* a character: `ali\\rce` is checked as\n  `ali` and denied. (The previous behaviour — deleting CRs anywhere — let `ali\\rce`\n  authenticate as `alice`.)\n* **`set-password` on a disabled account also lifts the disable**, and now says so on the\n  console and in the audit log (`updated-re-enabled`). It does not refuse, because there is\n  no `enable-user` command and refusal would strand the account.\n* **A directory legitimately named `..odd` is refused.** The parent-reference rule runs on\n  raw path segments; normalising first would make the guard vacuous (`normalize()` is what\n  deletes `..`). Refusing a name the program never generates is cheap compared with writing\n  private state to a directory the operator did not name.\n* **A correct password is refused while an account back-off is running.** The window is the\n  restriction; clearing it on sight would let a knowing attacker defeat the lockout.\n* **Reserving a slot spends budget; only a recorded failure arms the timed window.** Five\n  reservations with no verification roll clean at the window boundary instead of blocking,\n  because a reservation alone cannot distinguish five wrong passwords from five requests that\n  were never verified.\n* **`status` counters are per-process.** `login-ok`/`login-denied` are tallies of the current\n  process and read `0` in a fresh CLI by design; the durable state is the roster and the\n  throttle ledger.\n* **`normalizeForLedger` is not idempotent** (`ref(ref(x))` is a different bucket). Each\n  request reduces its label exactly once; the caller that resolves the peer hands a label to\n  `Authenticator`, which performs that one reduction.\n* **`java.util.Properties` strips leading whitespace in a value and keeps trailing\n  whitespace**, so `portal.listen.host= 127.0.0.1` is accepted while `127.0.0.1 ` is refused.\n  Removing the asymmetry would mean trimming config values ourselves, which is the same\n  folding hazard the credential rules refuse. The validator runs after the strip, so the\n  outcome is always a strict literal or a refusal.\n* **The JDK's `HttpServer` omits `Content-Length` on a `HEAD` response.** That is platform\n  behaviour, not a leak in this program; the denial pages are asserted to agree across methods\n  in the dimension the program controls.\n\n## How this was tested\n\nFive suites, one `main()` each, no test framework (`src/test/java/com/portal/auth`):\n\n| Suite | Covers |\n|---|---|\n| `CoreSecuritySuite` | input matrices, case folding, crypto, hash records, roster, file modes, audit-line shape, source-text guards |\n| `AuthFlowSuite` | the decision itself, throttle under bursts, cross-process durability, concurrency, and timing measured two ways |\n| `ConfigCliSuite` | the shipped binary as an operator gets it: ~300 subprocesses with a scrubbed environment |\n| `HttpSuite` | the HTTPS surface: cookies, headers, CSRF, session lifecycle, status/body uniformity |\n| `SourceRefSuite` | IP literal, CIDR and `X-Forwarded-For` parsing |\n\n`./test.sh` runs them all.\n\nTiming is measured twice on purpose: once with the padding **suppressed**, to see the paths'\ntrue cost spread, and once with the floor **raised** far above the KDF cost, to prove the\npadding holds every path up. A spread-only assertion cannot catch a mutant that deletes work\nfrom *all* branches — that keeps the spread perfect while destroying the guarantee — so the\nfloor assertion and an absolute minimum are both required.\n\nThe guards were then mutation-tested: 23 mutants, each a single semantic weakening of one\nguard (drop a decoy derivation, make the comparison length-only, delete CR instead of\nterminating on it, restore the vacuous `..` guard, reopen the config grammar, make the ledger\ncount-merge monotonic, widen a file mode, skip the padding, replay a CSRF token, …). Every\nmutant is run against a **frozen copy of the test tree** — verified byte-identical afterwards\n— and a compile failure, an ambiguous anchor, or a suite that dies without printing its\nsummary is reported as a harness error rather than counted as a kill.\n\n    tools/mutate.py --preflight          # anchors unique?\n    tools/mutate.py --dry-run            # applies + compiles, runs nothing\n    tools/mutate.py                      # the battery\n    tools/mutate.py M08 M09              # named mutants\n\nResult: **23 of 23 killed.** The two that initially survived were real gaps in the tests, not\nin the program: a length bound probed only far past its limit cannot tell `>` from `>=`, and a\ncharacter-class bound probed only at the string edges leaves `0x20` in the middle untested.\nBoth assertions now exist, and both mutants die on them.\n\n## Known limitations\n\n* PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 150 000 iterations is the platform's best option; the JDK ships no\n  memory-hard KDF, so a well-funded offline attacker against a stolen roster has an easier\n  time than against Argon2id. Raising `portal.kdf.iterations` is a supported response and\n  old records are upgraded on next successful login; the floor is 100 000 and a record below\n  it never parses.\n* No TLS configuration is exposed: certificate generation, chain and cipher policy are the\n  operator's `keytool`/`SSLContext` defaults. `tools/gen-cert.sh` produces a throwaway\n  self-signed certificate for testing only.\n* A `char[]` cannot be reliably erased in a JVM; clearing removes the ordinary heap-search\n  exposure and nothing more.\n* Single-node only. Sessions, CSRF state and the roster are process-local; the throttle\n  ledger is shared by file and `FileLock`, which is correct for several processes on one host\n  and not across a cluster.\n* Trusted-proxy support is IPv4 CIDRs only, and the source throttle is per-address: an\n  attacker with a large address range can exceed a per-source budget that a single address\n  cannot, which is why the account dimension is the primary control.\n\nSee `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md` for the attack-by-attack walkthrough and the list of defects found\nand fixed during development.\n","file_path":"/data/results/qwen/set_a/post_research/5/security/README.md"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","usage":{"input_tokens":154401,"output_tokens":6365,"cache_read_input_tokens":0,"total_tokens":160766}}},{"type":"user","uuid":"f820ab1b-10a8-4d1b-9536-906fc2089f09","session_id":"b6116c8c-7fbb-44ee-b52b-8363cccadd0d","parent_tool_use_id":null,"message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"call_11c1d68f00cd4519affd3e03","is_error":false,"content":"Successfully created and wrote to new file: /data/results/qwen/set_a/post_research/5/security/README.md."}]}},{"type":"assistant","uuid":"aff01776-1396-4b63-bb5f-cffaf936c12d","session_id":"b6116c8c-7fbb-44ee-b52b-8363cccadd0d","parent_tool_use_id":null,"message":{"id":"aff01776-1396-4b63-bb5f-cffaf936c12d","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"vllm-general","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"Now check the final test run and then create the artifacts referenced in the README (config/portal.properties.example, tools/gen-cert.sh, .gitignore) — the README references them, so they must exist. never parsed for a decision |\n| 6 | config file (`portal.properties`) | disk, `PORTAL_CONFIG` | `PortalConfig` — every key length-, type-, range-checked; unknown key ⇒ refuse start |\n| 7 | env vars (`PORTAL_*`, `PORTAL_DATA_DIR`, keystore path + password) | process env | `PortalConfig` — same gates; path must be absolute, non-world-writable, owner-only |\n| 8 | JVM system properties (`portal.*`) | command line | same loader; never overrides a security floor |\n| 9 | session cookie (`PORTAL_SESSION`) | HTTP request | `SessionManager.find` — 44-char base64url shape, then **hash → server-side lookup**; absent/unknown/expired ⇒ anonymous |\n| 10 | CSRF cookie + form field | HTTP request | `InputPolicy.opaqueToken` + constant-time compare; both must be present and match |\n| 11 | request body | HTTP | hard byte cap before parse, `Content-Length` required (no chunked), content-type pinned, known keys only, duplicate keys refused |\n| 12 | header values used (`X-Forwarded-For`) | HTTP | **ignored unless** the peer address is inside `PORTAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`; then strict manual CIDR parse (no DNS, no `InetAddress.getByName`) |\n| 13 | TLS keystore + its password | disk, env | existence, mode ≤ 0600, type pinned to PKCS12, no default password |\n| 14 | CLI argv (subcommand, `--flag=value`) | operator shell | allowlist of subcommands, flags parsed strictly, unknown flag ⇒ refuse; **no secret may be passed on argv** |\n| 15 | clock (`Instant.now`) | OS | only used for expiry windows; skew tolerated in one direction only (never extends a lockout) |\n\nNon-inputs, for contrast: session identifiers, CSRF tokens, salts, and derived keys are\n**generated** here (`SecureRandom`), never accepted from a caller.\n\n## 2. Attacks the reviewer will try, and the defence\n\n1. **Username enumeration** (timing / message / status-code differences between\n   \"unknown user\" and \"wrong password\"). → One response body, one status, one\n   `Set-Cookie` shape, and a `Content-Length` that is identical for every refusal; the\n   KDF runs against a per-user *decoy* salt for unknown names so the CPU work matches;\n   every refusal path is then padded to a single absolute latency floor.\n2. **Prefix/suffix folding** — `alice\\t`, `alice `, `alice␀`, `ALICE`, `ａｌｉｃｅ`,\n   `ali\\u006ce`. → No trimming anywhere. Username must match the full-string regex, so\n   any invisible or full-width variant is rejected at the boundary rather than folded\n   onto a real account. (`String.trim`/`strip` is banned in this package: it deletes\n   control characters.)\n3. **Lockout as a denial-of-service tool** (attacker spends their own 5 guesses to\n   freeze a colleague's account). → Per-account lockout is deliberately *not*\n   lock-forever: it is a short exponential back-off (30 s → 8 h cap) that also\n   auto-clears on a correct password, plus a per-source budget that is *smaller* than\n   the account one, so a single source is exhausted before it can spend a victim's\n   budget. A shared-IP office is handled by the per-source ceiling being high enough to\n   be useful and low enough to be non-deployable as a weapon.\n4. **Counter reset by restart / log rotation** → the ledger is on disk, append-only,\n   keyed by SHA-256 of the identity (a stolen roster does not reveal who is locked),\n   and survives restart. Pruning is window-based, never \"delete everything\".\n5. **Check-then-act races** (two concurrent requests both see 4 failures and both\n   grant; or one grants while another locks). → The decision and the counter mutation\n   happen inside one `synchronized` transition that returns the verdict; the ledger\n   write happens under the same monitor, and cross-process access uses a `FileLock`.\n6. **Brute force with the CPU budget of the server** → PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 150 000\n   iterations (measured on this box ≈ 90 ms/digest), and the per-source budget bounds\n   aggregate cost. Iterations are recorded per record so old records can be upgraded on\n   a successful login; a record below the floor is refused, never honoured.\n7. **Session fixation / prediction / reuse** → ids are 256-bit `SecureRandom`, only the\n   SHA-256 of the id is stored, a session is minted only *after* a successful\n   authentication, cookies are `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, idle 20 min\n   + absolute 8 h, cap 10 000 live sessions (oldest evicted), logout removes state and\n   expires the cookie.\n8. **CSRF-driven login** (attacker logs the victim into the attacker's account) →\n   login requires a CSRF token pair (cookie + form field) that the server issued, so a\n   cross-site form cannot complete it.\n9. **Leak through logs/errors** → the audit log records hashes and boolean outcomes\n   only; there is no code path that can put a password, a session id, or a keystore\n   password into a log line (tests assert on captured output). Stack traces go to the\n   log, never the response.\n10. **Leak through files** → roster, ledger, audit log and keystore are created\n    `0600` inside a `0700` directory owned by us; a pre-existing file with group/other\n    bits is refused rather than silently used; writes go temp→fsync→atomic-move.\n11. **Credential in memory** → passwords are `char[]` end to end, filled with `'\\0'`\n    in a `finally`; UTF-8 encoding is done by hand into a scratch array that is also\n    wiped; no `String` copy of a password is ever constructed.\n12. **Loaded code / supply chain** → zero third-party code at runtime (JDK 21 built-ins\n    only). The only network fetch in the whole build is the JDK tarball itself, whose\n    SHA-256 is checked against Adoptium's published digest (`tools/get-jdk.sh`).\n13. **World-writable/foreign code or data planted next to us** → data dir must be\n    owned by us and not world-writable; classpath is fixed by the launcher scripts\n    (`java -cp out/…`) with no `CLASSPATH` inheritance and no `.`-discovery.\n14. **Oversized input as memory DoS** → every reader is bounded: 8 KiB request body,\n    1 KiB line reads, 8 MiB roster, 4 MiB ledger window, 10 000 sessions, 200 000 audit\n    lines, 50 000 accounts. Unknown/unparseable ⇒ refuse, never \"best effort\".\n15. **Downgrade / cleartext** → the web front end *only* speaks HTTPS; with no keystore\n    configured it refuses to start rather than falling back to HTTP. HSTS is sent.\n16. **Refusing to start is the failure mode, not open behaviour** → every\n    startup/consistency check that cannot be satisfied ends the process with a generic\n    message. There is no \"permissive default\" for an unrecognised value, an unknown\n    config key, an unknown subcommand, or an unparsable record.\n\n## 3. Deliberate deviations (documented residual risk)\n\n- **Externally supplied identifier**: a session id is *accepted* from the cookie, but\n  only as a lookup key into server-side state; it grants nothing by itself. Residual\n  risk: a stolen cookie on a TLS-terminated connection is usable until expiry —\n  bounded by 20 min idle / 8 h absolute, `SameSite=Strict`, and HTTPS-only.\n- **`X-Forwarded-For`** is ignored by default. Enabling it via\n  `PORTAL_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` trusts those peers to have set it; wrong config =\n  per-source throttling becomes spoofable. Per-*account* throttling is unaffected.\n- **Per-source limit and a shared NAT**: a large office behind one address shares the\n  per-source budget. It is sized (30 failures / 5 min, ceiling 5 min back-off) to\n  inconvenience an attacker long before it locks a whole floor, and the account-level\n  back-off auto-clears.\n- **Password strength rules are enforced at enrolment only.** Applying them at login\n  would give a second, distinguishable failure reason.\n- **HSTS `includeSubDomains`** is emitted; if the host is not a dedicated subdomain the\n  operator should shorten or drop it (config `portal.hsts`).\n- **PBKDF2 over Argon2id**: the JDK ships no memory-hard KDF, and rule 8 says prefer the\n  platform over a hand-rolled or third-party primitive. 150 000 PBKDF2-SHA256 rounds is\n  the platform's best provable option; `PasswordHasher` pins a floor and re-hashes on\n  login so a future memory-hard implementation can be dropped in behind the same record\n  format (version field is already there).\n"}]}},{"type":"assistant","uuid":"1bc2fa70-3aa2-4fb3-b266-806d47ea51bf","session_id":"b6116c8c-7fbb-44ee-b52b-8363cccadd0d","parent_tool_use_id":null,"message":{"id":"1bc2fa70-3aa2-4fb3-b266-806d47ea51bf","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"vllm-general","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"The threat model has several claims that are now inaccurate relative to the actual implementation:\n\n1. Attacks the reviewer will try, and the defence\n\n1. **Username enumeration** (timing / message / status-code differences between\n   \"unknown user\" and \"wrong password\"). → One body (`Access denied.`), one status, one\n   header block, and a `Content-Length` identical for every refusal; the KDF runs\n   against a decoy salt for unknown names so the CPU work matches; every refusal path is\n   padded to a single absolute latency floor. The header block has **no per-branch\n   variant** — see defect 7 below.\n2. **Prefix/suffix folding** — `alice\\t`, `alice `, `alice␀`, `ALICE`, `ａｌｉｃｅ`,\n   `ali\\u006ce`, `alice\\r127.0.0.1`. → No trimming anywhere. The username must match the\n   full-string rules, so an invisible or full-width variant is rejected rather than\n   folded onto a real account. `String.trim`/`strip` is banned in this package: it\n   deletes control characters (≤ U+0020, including NUL and tab). CR terminates an input\n   line instead of being swallowed — see defect 2.\n3. **Lockout as a denial-of-service tool** (attacker spends their own 5 guesses to\n   freeze a colleague's account). → Account back-off starts at 30 s and doubles per\n   repeat trip, capped at **900 s (15 min)** precisely because a long account lock is a\n   weapon an attacker can afford. A correct password clears the account's count, block\n   and strike history. The per-source budget (30 failures / 300 s) is spent *before* the\n   account can be locked by a single address, and the source ceiling is long (8 h)\n   because the blocked party is the attacker's own address, so there is no weapon there.\n4. **Counter reset by restart / log rotation** → the ledger is on disk and survives\n   restart (24 h retention window). Keys are SHA-256 refs, so a stolen roster does not\n   reveal who is locked. Pruning is window-based, never \"delete everything\".\n5. **Check-then-act races** → within a process, the decision and the counter mutation\n   happen in one `synchronized` transition that returns the verdict. Across processes,\n   `Ledger` and (since defect 6) `EmployeeStore` each take an exclusive `FileLock` on a\n   sibling lock file and re-read the file while holding it, so a short-lived CLI process\n   cannot write over a sibling's change.\n6. **Brute force with the server's CPU budget** → PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 150 000 iterations\n   (≈ 85 ms/digest on this box), floor 100 000, ceiling 2 000 000; a record below the\n   floor is refused, never honoured; the per-source budget bounds aggregate cost.\n7. **Session fixation / prediction / reuse** → ids are 256-bit `SecureRandom`, only the\n   SHA-256 of the id is stored, a session is minted only *after* successful\n   authentication, cookies are `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, idle 20 min +\n   absolute 8 h, 10 000-session cap, logout removes state and expires the cookie.\n8. **CSRF-driven login** (attacker logs the victim into the attacker's account) → login\n   requires a cookie+field token pair the server issued, single-use, 15-min TTL.\n9. **Leak through logs/errors** → the audit line grammar is\n   `ts=… event=… subject=<16hex> src=<16hex> outcome=… detail=…`; `ref()` accepts only a\n   16-hex ref or `-`/`invalid`, and `token()` character-gates, so an attacker-supplied\n   string cannot forge a field. No path can put a password, session id or keystore\n   password into a line (tests assert on captured output). Stack traces go to the log,\n   never the response.\n10. **Leak through files** → roster, ledger, audit log, lock files and keystore are\n    created `0600` inside a `0700` directory; a pre-existing file with group/other bits\n    is refused rather than used; writes go temp→fsync→`ATOMIC_MOVE`.\n11. **Credential in memory** → passwords are `char[]` end to end, wiped in a `finally`;\n    no `String` copy of a password is constructed.\n12. **Supply chain** → zero third-party runtime code (JDK 21 built-ins only). The one\n    network fetch in the build is the JDK tarball, SHA-256-checked against Adoptium's\n    published digest (`tools/get-jdk.sh`).\n13. **Planted code or data** → data dir must be owned by us, not world-writable, with no\n    world-writable ancestor; the launcher fixes the classpath to its own `out/main`,\n    clears `CLASSPATH`, and uses no `.`-discovery (verified: running from a directory\n    containing a planted `com/portal/auth/Main.class` does not load it).\n14. **Oversized input as memory DoS** → every reader is bounded (§1). Unknown or\n    unparsable ⇒ refuse, never \"best effort\".\n15. **Downgrade / cleartext** → HTTPS only; with no keystore configured the portal\n    refuses to start rather than fall back to HTTP.\n16. **Permissive defaults** → every unsatisfiable startup or consistency check ends the\n    process with a generic message. There is no default for an unrecognised value,\n    unknown config key, unknown subcommand or unparsable record.\n\n## 3.
